Once upon a time there was a girl called Anna. She was three years old and loved to explore the world.

Anna ran and ran, but when she noticed she was going to lose the race, she stopped. She noticed the wide sky, saw the clouds in the shape of animals and felt proud of herself. She had raced herself, and that was enough. 

Anna smiled and ran back home, happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a cottage deep in the forest. Every day, he would go out and collect wood from the forest so he could keep warm in his house. One day, as he was gathering wood, a strange creature appeared in front of him. It had long, pointy ears and a wrinkly face.

The creature demanded that the old man give it some silver. The old man was scared, but he had no silver coins. So, he said he couldn't give the creature what it asked for. The creature got angry and started shouting at the old man.

Fortunately, a kindly elderly lady appeared and saw what was going on. She quickly ran over to the old man and gave him a small pouch of silver coins. She said they were hers, but the old man could keep them if the creature demanded silver.

The creature was very pleased with this and soon left the old man and the elderly lady alone. From then on, the old man was very careful with the silver coins. He had learned his lesson about not giving away all his money.

Once upon a time there was a little monkey. His name was Blink. One day he decided to explore the ancient forest. He followed the trail deep into the forest, blinking his eyes in amazement at all the ancient beings that lived there.

He saw many different types of birds, animals, and plants. They were so old and wise. He watched them move from tree to tree, or hop across the trail. They whispered secrets in the breeze.

Suddenly, Blink heard a rumble and the ground shook beneath him. He looked around and saw an ancient volcano erupting! He was so scared. But the little monkey bravely followed the trail out of the forest, blinking with fear.

At last, he emerged from the forest safely. He was never so glad to be back in the open air. He vowed to never go on such a dangerous adventure again.

The End.

The other bees said, "You can't do that! It's not safe." But the bee kept poking the hive.

The bee lost his home and all of his friends. He felt really sad. He realized he should never have poked the hive.

The crane replied, "Oh, that is very sad. I can teach you how to fly if you like." The little girl looked up with a glimmer of hope in her eyes and wiped her tears away.

Lila and Ben liked to look at the stars at night. They had a big book with pictures of stars and planets and moons. They learned the names of some of them, like Sun and Earth and Mars. But their favorite thing to see was a comet. A comet was a bright ball of ice and dust that flew across the sky with a long tail. Sometimes, comets only came once in a long time, and sometimes they never came back.

One night, Lila and Ben saw a poster on the window of a toy shop. It said: "Sell comet toys! Only for one week! Hurry up and get yours!" The poster had a picture of a shiny comet with a smiley face and a button that made it light up and make sounds. Lila and Ben wanted a comet toy very much. They ran to their mom and dad and asked them if they could buy one.

Mom and dad looked at the poster and smiled. They said: "We have a surprise for you. Tomorrow night, there will be a real comet in the sky. It is very rare and special. It is called Halley's Comet. It only comes once every 76 years. We have a telescope that we can use to see it better. How about we go to the park and watch it together?"

Lila and Ben were very happy and excited. They said: "Yes, yes, yes! We want to see the real comet! Thank you, mom and dad!" They hugged their parents and went to bed early. They dreamed of the comet and how jolly it would be.

The next night, they went to the park with their mom and dad and their telescope. They set it up on a hill and waited for the comet to appear. They saw many stars and some planes and a moon, but no comet. They started to feel sad and bored. They said: "Where is the comet? When will it come? Maybe the poster was right and we should have bought a comet toy instead."

Mom and dad said: "Don't worry, children. The comet will come soon. It is just behind that cloud. You have to be patient and keep looking. The real comet is much more beautiful and amazing than any toy. You will see."

Just then, the cloud moved and they saw a bright streak of light in the sky. It was the comet! It was bigger and brighter and more colorful than they had imagined. It had a long tail that sparkled and waved. It made a soft sound like a whistle. It looked like it was smiling at them. Lila and Ben gasped and clapped and cheered. They said: "Wow! Look at the comet! It is so jolly! It is the best thing we ever saw! We are so glad we did not buy a comet toy. This is much better!"

Mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said: "We are glad too. This is a special night that we will always remember. We are lucky to see the comet together. We love you, Lila and Ben."

They watched the comet for a long time, until it faded away. They packed their telescope and went home. They felt happy and warm inside. They knew they had seen something wonderful. They knew they had a jolly comet story to tell.

One day, she flew near a big clock. The clock was on a tall tower. It had a face with two hands and a bell. The clock told the time with a loud ding-dong. Lily was nosy. She wanted to see the clock up close. She flew closer and closer to the tower.

"Hello, little girl," said the clock. "What are you doing here?"

"I'm flying with my balloon," said Lily. "You are a big clock. Can I see your face?"

"Sure, you can," said the clock. "But be careful. Don't touch my hands or my bell. They are very important. They tell the time for everyone."

Lily nodded. She flew near the clock's face. She saw the numbers and the hands. She saw the bell behind the face. She was very curious. She reached out her hand to touch the bell.

"No, don't do that!" shouted the clock. "You will make a big noise and scare everyone!"

But it was too late. Lily touched the bell and it rang loudly. Ding-dong, ding-dong, ding-dong! The sound was so loud that Lily's balloon popped. She fell down from the sky. She was scared and sad.

The clock felt sorry for Lily. He called for help. A kind man saw Lily falling and caught her in his arms. He was a fireman. He had a ladder and a truck. He took Lily down from the tower and gave her a hug.

"Are you okay, little girl?" he asked.

"I'm okay, thank you," said Lily. "But my balloon is gone. I can't fly anymore."

"I'm sorry about your balloon," said the fireman. "But you know, flying is not safe for little girls. You could get hurt or lost. You should stay on the ground and play with your friends."

Lily nodded. She understood. She was sorry for being nosy and touching the clock. She said sorry to the clock and the fireman. They forgave her and smiled.

"Goodbye, big clock," she said. "Thank you for telling the time. Maybe I will see you again, but from far away."

"Goodbye, little girl," said the clock. "Thank you for visiting me. Maybe you will see me again, but from close up."

Lily smiled. She learned a lesson. She was still nosy, but she was also careful. She liked to fly, but she also liked to walk. She had fun with her new balloon and her friends. She was happy.

Lily and Ben said, "Thank you, Mom." They ate their lunch. They liked the beef. It was tasty. They were happy. They learned their lesson. They did not reach for the beef again.

Lily was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new places. One day, she saw a big tree with red apples in the garden. She wanted to pick some apples and eat them. She asked her mom if she could go to the tree.

Mom said, "Yes, you can go, but be careful. And only pick three apples. Can you count to three?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I can count to three. One, two, three." She ran to the tree and climbed up. She saw many apples and they looked yummy. She picked one apple and put it in her basket. She counted, "One."

She picked another apple and put it in her basket. She counted, "Two."

She picked a third apple and put it in her basket. She counted, "Three."

But then she saw a bigger and redder apple on a higher branch. She wanted that apple too. She thought, "Maybe I can pick one more. Mom won't notice." She reached for the apple, but it was too far. She lost her balance and fell down. She hurt her arm and cried.

Mom heard her cry and ran to her. She saw Lily on the ground with her basket and four apples. She hugged her and said, "Are you okay, Lily? What happened?"

Lily sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted one more apple. I didn't listen to you. I was greedy."

Mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you're not badly hurt. But you should have followed my rule. I told you to pick only three apples. You should be happy with what you have and not want more than you need. That's called being grateful. Can you say grateful?"

Lily repeated, "Grateful."

Mom said, "Good. Now let's go inside and wash your arm. And we can share the apples with your brother and sister. They will be happy too. And you can count the apples again. How many apples do we have?"

Lily counted, "One, two, three, four."

Mom said, "That's right. And how many people do we have?"

Lily counted, "One, two, three, four."

Mom said, "That's right. So we can each have one apple. And that's enough. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I'm sorry and I'm grateful. I love you, Mom."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You're my adventurous girl. But sometimes you need to be careful and listen to me. That's called being wise. Can you say wise?"

Lily repeated, "Wise."

Mom said, "Good. Now let's go and enjoy our apples."

The end.

Ben was sad. He liked the stick. He said, "Lily, why did you do that? That was our pole. Now we can't play with it anymore. And you scared the fish. They are hidden now. That was not nice."

Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Of course I forgive you, Lily. You are my friend. But next time, let's be more careful and kind. Maybe the fish will come back and play with us."

Lily nodded and hugged Ben back. She said, "You are my friend too, Ben. And you are very wise. Next time, let's be more careful and kind. Maybe the fish will come back and play with us."

Moral value: The story teaches the value of patience, gentleness, and friendship. It also shows the consequences of anger, violence, and waste.

Rory did not hear her. He was too busy stretching. He said, "Look, Lila. I can stretch my horn so high that I can touch the sky!"

He ran around the jungle, trying to get rid of the pepper. He bumped into trees, rocks, and other animals. He made a lot of noise and trouble. Lila followed him, trying to help him. She said, "Rory, calm down! You have to spit out the pepper! It is spicy! It is not good for you!"

Lila said, "It's okay, Rory. I know you did not mean it. You are a good stretcher, but you have to be careful. Sometimes, stretching too much can get you into trouble."

Tom was not okay. He was sad and angry. He said, "No, I'm not okay. You made me reverse my car and now it's broken. It's all your fault!"

Lily did not like being blamed. She said, "No, it's not my fault. You agreed to reverse your car. You should have been more careful."

They started to argue and shout. They forgot about the sun and the race. They only cared about their cars and their feelings.

The sun was almost gone. It was very dark and cold. They heard their mom calling them from the house. She said, "Tom, Lily, come inside. It's time for dinner and bed."

They stopped arguing and looked at each other. They realized they had wasted their time and their fun. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "Mom, we're coming. We're sorry."

They picked up their cars and walked to the house. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They learned their lesson. They learned that playing fair and being kind is more important than winning and being fast. They learned that the sun does not wait for anyone. They learned to enjoy the sun while it shines.

She went to Ben's house and knocked on the door. Ben opened the door and smiled.

"Hi, Lily! What do you have?" he asked.

"Hi, Ben! I have a flute. Do you want to see?" Lily said.

"Yes, please! Can I try it?" Ben said.

Lily nodded and gave him the flute. She showed him how to hold it and blow into it.

Ben tried to play the flute, but he was clumsy. He dropped the flute on the floor and made a loud noise.

"Oh, no! I'm sorry, Lily! I broke your flute!" Ben said.

Lily looked at the flute. It was not broken, but it had a dent.

"It's okay, Ben. It still works. See?" Lily said. She picked up the flute and played a tune.

Ben listened and clapped.

"Wow, Lily! You are good at playing the flute! Can you teach me?" Ben said.

Lily smiled and nodded.

"Sure, Ben. I can teach you. But first, let me introduce you to someone. This is Fluffy, my flute. He likes to make music with me. Say hi, Fluffy!" Lily said.

She held the flute near Ben's face and made it squeak.

"Hi, Fluffy!" Ben said, laughing.

Lily and Ben became good friends. They played music and had fun with Fluffy the flute.

"Look at that boat!" Sam said, pointing to a red boat with a big sail. "It is so pretty and fast. I wish I had a boat like that."

"Me too," Pat said. "But we can't touch the real boats. They are not ours. They belong to other people."

Sam and Pat walked along the port, looking at the boats. They saw a blue boat with a tough metal hull. It looked strong and sturdy. Sam had an idea.

"Let's play with this boat," he said. "It is tough and can't break. No one will mind if we play with it for a little while."

Pat was not sure. He looked around and saw no one near the boat. He wanted to play with the boat, but he also knew it was wrong.

"I don't know, Sam," he said. "This is not our boat. We should not touch it. What if someone gets angry at us?"

Sam did not listen. He climbed onto the boat and started to push buttons and pull levers. He pretended he was the captain of the boat. He made noises like a boat horn and a boat engine.

"Come on, Pat," he said. "This is fun. Don't be scared. No one will see us."

Pat hesitated, but he followed Sam. He climbed onto the boat and joined him in playing. They had fun for a while, until they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing on my boat? Get off right now!"

Sam and Pat turned and saw a man running towards them. He looked angry and scary. He was the owner of the boat. He had seen them from a distance and came to stop them.

Sam and Pat were frightened. They jumped off the boat and ran away. They did not say sorry to the man. They did not look back. They ran all the way home.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should not touch things that are not theirs. They learned that they should respect other people's property. They learned that playing with real boats is not as fun as playing with toy boats. They learned that being tough is not as important as being good.

One day, her brother Max came into her room. He saw her drawings and said, "These are silly. Ink is for writing, not drawing. You should use crayons or pencils. And why do you draw so big? Your drawings don't fit on the paper. They go over the edges and make a mess."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, ink is for drawing too. I like to draw big because I have big ideas. And I don't make a mess. I'm careful with the ink."

Max said, "No, you're not. Look, you spilled some ink on the floor. And on your bed. And on your shirt. You're a bad drawer and a bad sister."

Lily cried and ran out of the room. She went to the kitchen and told her mom what Max said. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't listen to him, Lily. You're a good drawer and a good sister. You have a lot of talent and imagination. And ink is a wonderful medium for art. You just need to be more careful with it. Why don't you use a bigger paper or a smaller brush? Or maybe you can use a tray or a mat to protect the floor and the bed. And you can wear an apron or an old shirt to protect your clothes."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You're right. I can do that. Can I show you my drawings?"

Her mom said, "Of course, honey. I would love to see them. Let's go to your room and clean up the ink first. And maybe we can talk to Max and make him understand why you like to draw with ink."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Let's go." She took her mom's hand and they went to her room. She hoped that Max would be nice to her and her drawings. She still liked to draw with ink. She could imagine anything and make it on paper. She was very happy.

Suddenly, the witch flew down to them and said, "Hello, children! I'm not a real witch, I'm just a person in a costume. I'm here to give you some candy!" The children were happy and thanked the witch for the candy.

After that, Lily's friend said, "I still think witches are terrible." But Lily said, "I don't think so, they can be friendly too!" And they all laughed and continued playing in the park. The end.

The bear continued to walk in the forest and found a beehive. The bear tried to reach the honey, but he couldn't. The bear remembered the butterfly and thought that if he could fly, he could reach the honey. The bear decided to ask the butterfly for help. The bear said sorry to the butterfly for scaring her earlier and asked if she could help him. The butterfly agreed and carried the bear to the beehive. The bear got the honey and thanked the butterfly for her help. From that day on, the bear and the butterfly became friends and flew together in the sky.

The lady smiles. "Yes, it is. Geckos are very special. They can stick to walls and change colors. They are also very shy. They do not like to be touched or chased. They run away when they feel scared."

Tim and Sam understand. They feel sorry for the gecko. They did not mean to scare it.

"We are sorry, lizard lady," Tim says. "We did not know. We just wanted to see the gecko."

The lady nods. She is not angry. She is happy that they like lizards.

Tim and Sam nod. They understand. They promise to be careful and respectful with lizards.

The lady smiles. She gives them a sticker of a gecko. They say thank you and goodbye. They go back to the park. They play with their sticker. They are happy. They love lizards.

After Daisy made her mark in the snow, she heard a voice saying. "Hey you, what are you doing?" Daisy looked up and saw a squirrel watching her. Daisy was a bit scared, but she said, "What's the matter?"

The squirrel replied, "You don't need to mark your spot, I was here first." Daisy wasn't sure what the squirrel meant at first. Then the squirrel explained that it had made the marks in the snow earlier. Daisy was so pleased to have made a new friend in the winter. Daisy said goodbye to the squirrel and from that day on, Daisy no longer marked her spot in the winter.

Hannah's dad saw the worry in her eyes and called back to her, "Don't worry - I will come back and get it."

Once the luggage was safely onboard, they were on their way! They were off to their big adventure!

Lily didn't want to stop playing her drum, but she knew she had to listen to her mom. So she shut the door and continued playing.

But then, Lily's little brother came into the room and started dancing around. He accidentally knocked over the drum and it broke into pieces.

Lily was very upset and started crying. Her mom came in and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You can always get a new drum. But remember to be more graceful next time and not make too much noise."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and keep them in her drawer. One day, Lily's mom asked her to go to bed because it was getting dark outside. 

Lily said, "But I want to keep playing with my toys." 

Her mom replied, "You can keep playing tomorrow, Lily. It's time for bed now." 

Lily went to her room and opened her drawer. She saw that one of her toys was missing. She said, "Mom, where is my toy?" 

Her mom said, "I put it away because it was too light outside to see it." 

Lily felt sad but her mom gave her a big hug and said, "Don't worry, you can play with it tomorrow." 

Lily went to bed with a smile on her face, knowing that her toy was safe in her drawer.

Lily said, "Hi, Mr. Snowman! Can I touch your hat?" 

The snowman replied, "Yes, you can touch it. But be careful, it's cold!" 

Lily touched the carrot hat and felt the cold snow on her fingers. She laughed and said, "That's so cool! Can I touch your scarf too?" 

The snowman smiled and said, "Of course! It's made of sticks, so it won't be as cold." 

Lily touched the stick scarf and felt how different it was from the carrot hat. She thanked the snowman and went back inside to warm up. From that day on, Lily visited the unique snowman every time it snowed.

The little fish swam up to Susie and said, "Don't worry! I will help you save yourself!" Using its tiny fins, the fish struggled to push Susie up to the surface. 

After a few minutes, Susie was finally back on shore. She gave the fish a big kiss and thanked it for saving her. From that day on, Susie and the little fish were the best of friends. They would swim together every day and explore the beautiful lake.

"Let me go, let me go!" the beetle said. But Lily did not understand. She held the beetle tighter.

"Ouch, that hurt!" Lily said. She rubbed her finger. She felt sad and angry. "Bad beetle, bad beetle!"

Tim saw what happened. He felt sorry for Lily and the beetle. He ran to the beetle and picked it up. He put it back on the leaf.

"Sorry, beetle," Tim said. "Lily did not mean to hurt you. She just wanted to be your friend."

"Thank you, thank you!" the beetle said. "You are a good boy. You are my new friend."

Tim smiled. He was happy to help the beetle. He waved to the beetle and went back to Lily.

Lily nodded. She felt better too. She smiled at Tim and the beetle.

"I'm sorry, beetle," Lily said. "You are a nice beetle. You are my new friend too."

"Oh no!" Ben and Mia say together. They are scared and sad. They broke Mommy's glass.

Mommy hears the ring sound. She comes to the kitchen. She sees the broken glass on the floor. She sees Ben and Mia with their eyes wide and their mouths open.

"What happened here?" she asks.

Ben and Mia look at each other. They do not know what to say. They are sorry for breaking the glass. They know Mommy will be mad.

Mommy sees their faces. She knows they did not mean to break the glass. She is not mad. She is glad they are not hurt. The glass is tough, but it can cut them.

"It's okay, Ben and Mia. I know you were curious. But you have to be careful with glass. It is not a toy. It can break and hurt you. Next time, ask me before you touch it, okay?" she says.

Ben and Mia nod. They say sorry to Mommy. They hug her. Mommy hugs them back. She tells them she loves them. She helps them clean up the mess. She gives them a new glass. It is plastic. It is not shiny and clear. But it is not tough. It does not break. It does not ring. Ben and Mia like it. They drink water from it. They are happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily was bored at home. She had no toys to play with, no books to read, and no friends to visit. Her mom was busy in the kitchen, and her dad was at work. Lily felt very dull.

She decided to wander around the house, looking for something fun. She opened doors and drawers, but found nothing interesting. She went upstairs and downstairs, but saw nothing new. She went to the backyard, but it was too cold and wet.

She came back inside and saw a door she had never opened before. It was in the hallway, next to the bathroom. She was curious and tried to turn the knob, but it was locked. She wondered what was behind the door. Maybe it was a secret room, or a treasure chest, or a magic portal.

She looked around and saw a key on a hook. It was shiny and silver, and had a funny shape. She reached for it and took it off the hook. She ran to the door and tried to fit the key in the lock. It was hard, but she managed to turn it. She heard a click and pushed the door open.

She gasped and smiled. Behind the door was a big closet, full of colorful clothes, hats, shoes, and accessories. There were dresses and skirts, shirts and pants, coats and scarves, boots and sandals, hats and crowns, necklaces and bracelets, and more. Lily felt like she had found a wonderland.

She quickly forgot about her boredom and started to try on different outfits. She pretended to be a princess, a pirate, a superhero, a dancer, and a clown. She had so much fun, she didn't hear her mom calling her for lunch. She didn't notice the time passing by. She didn't see her dad coming home from work.

She only stopped when she heard a knock on the door. She opened it and saw her mom and dad, looking surprised and amused. They saw her wearing a pink tutu, a yellow raincoat, a green hat, and a purple necklace. They laughed and hugged her.

"Lily, what are you doing in here?" her mom asked.

"I was wandering and I found this lock and this key and this closet and all these clothes and I was playing and having fun and I'm sorry I didn't hear you and I love you and can I keep this hat?" Lily said in one breath.

Her mom and dad smiled and kissed her.

"Of course you can, sweetie. You look wonderful. But now it's time for lunch. Come on, let's go downstairs. And maybe later we can play together in the closet. How does that sound?" her dad said.

Lily nodded and grinned. She took off the hat and put it on her dad's head. She held her mom's hand and followed them downstairs. She felt very happy. She had found a new way to have fun, and she had made her parents laugh. She thought that wandering was not so dull after all.

One day, she zoomed to the park. She saw a big tree with a hole. She zoomed closer and looked inside. She saw a small brown animal with a long tail. It was a squirrel. The squirrel had a big nut in its mouth. It looked at Lily and smiled.

"Hello, little girl," the squirrel said. "Do you want to share my nut?"

"Hello, little squirrel," Lily said. "What is your name?"

"My name is Nibbles," the squirrel said. "I live in this tree. I collect nuts and store them for winter. I am a wise squirrel. I know many things."

Lily was impressed. She wanted to be wise too. She wanted to learn many things.

"What can you teach me, Nibbles?" Lily asked.

Nibbles thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"I can teach you how to make chocolate," he said.

Lily's eyes widened. She loved chocolate. She wanted to know how to make it.

"Really?" she asked. "How do you make chocolate?"

Nibbles smiled. He had a plan.

"Follow me," he said. "I will show you."

He jumped out of the hole and ran to his bike. He had a bike too. It was small and red. He had found it in a trash can. He had fixed it and painted it.

"Come on, Lily," he said. "Let's zoom to the store. We need some ingredients."

"Good job, Nibbles," Lily said. "You are very smart."

"Thank you, Lily," Nibbles said. "You are very kind."

They zoomed back to the park. They went to the tree. They mixed the ingredients in a pot. They put the pot on a fire. They stirred and stirred. They made chocolate.

"Wow, Nibbles," Lily said. "You are amazing. You made chocolate."

"Thank you, Lily," Nibbles said. "You are wonderful. You helped me."

"Can we eat it, Nibbles?" she asked.

"Of course, Lily," Nibbles said. "We can share it. You are my friend."

They broke the chocolate squirrel in half. They each took a bite. They smiled. It was delicious.

They ate the chocolate squirrel. They were happy. They were full. They were wise. They zoomed away.

Later that day, Lily and Mittens went for a walk. They saw a big dog who was also black. The dog came up to them and Lily was a little scared. But Mittens just shrugged and rubbed against the dog's leg. The dog was friendly and they all became friends. They walked together and found a park where they played with a ball. Then they went back home and had some more sausages for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends and explore the world around her. One day, Lily and her friends saw a big hill in the distance. The hill was so high that they couldn't see the top.

Lily and her friends decided to climb the hill to see what was at the top. It was a long and tiring climb, but they kept going. When they finally reached the top, they saw a beautiful garden filled with colorful flowers. They were so happy to have made it to the top.

Suddenly, they heard a voice say "Welcome to my garden." It was the owner of the garden, an old lady who had been watching them climb. She was very kind and showed them around her garden. Lily and her friends were so happy to have made a new friend and to have discovered such a beautiful place. From that day on, they visited the garden often and enjoyed the view from the high hill.

One day, an otter named Ollie was playing with his friends in the river. They liked to slide on the rocks, catch fish, and splash each other. Ollie was very good at sliding, and he always went the fastest.

"Look at me, I'm the best slider!" he said to his friends. "No one can pass me!"

But then he saw a new otter in the water. She was smaller than him, but she was very fast too. She slid on the rocks and passed Ollie with a smile.

"Hi, I'm Oona," she said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Ollie felt angry and sad. He did not like that Oona passed him. He thought he was the best slider. He did not want to play with her.

"No, I don't want to play with you," he said. "You are not my friend. You are too fast."

Oona looked sad too. She did not mean to make Ollie angry. She just wanted to have fun and make a new friend.

"I'm sorry, I did not know you were mad," she said. "I just like to slide. It's not important who is faster. It's important who is nicer."

Ollie thought about what Oona said. He realized that she was right. It was not important who was faster. It was important who was nicer. He felt sorry for being mean to Oona.

"I'm sorry too," he said. "I was not nice to you. You are a good slider. And you are a good otter. Do you want to be my friend?"

Oona smiled and nodded. She was happy that Ollie was nice to her. She wanted to be his friend.

"Yes, I want to be your friend," she said. "Let's play together. We can slide, catch fish, and splash each other. And we can share our rocks."

Ollie and Oona became friends. They played with each other and with the other otters. They had a lot of fun. And they learned that it was not important who was faster. It was important who was nicer.

Lily was sick. She had a hot head and a sore throat. Mommy took her to the doctor. The doctor was kind. He smiled and said hello to Lily.

First, the doctor weighed Lily on a big scale. He said, "You are a big girl, Lily. You weigh 15 kilos." Lily felt proud. She liked being big.

Then, the doctor put a thermometer in Lily's mouth. He said, "This will tell me how hot you are. You have to wait a little bit." Lily waited. She felt the thermometer under her tongue. It was cold and hard.

The thermometer beeped. The doctor looked at it. He said, "You have a fever, Lily. You are 39 degrees. That is too hot. You need some medicine to make you feel better." He gave Lily a spoon of syrup. It was sweet and sticky.

Lily swallowed the syrup. She said, "Thank you, doctor. Will I be well soon?" The doctor nodded. He said, "Yes, Lily. You will be well soon. You have to rest and drink lots of water. And you have to take the syrup twice a day." He gave Mommy a bottle of syrup.

Mommy thanked the doctor. She said, "You are very kind, doctor. You helped Lily a lot." She took Lily's hand and they went home. Lily felt a little better. She hoped she would be well soon. She hugged Mommy and said, "I love you, Mommy. You are kind too." Mommy kissed Lily and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my brave girl."

Tom and Mia were hungry. They wanted to eat lunch. Mom said they could have beans and bread. Tom liked beans. Mia did not like beans. She said beans were yucky.

"Please try some beans, Mia," Mom said. "Beans are good for you. They make you strong and powerful."

Mia shook her head. She did not want to try beans. She wanted to eat something else. She looked at Tom. He was eating his beans. He smiled at her.

"Beans are yummy, Mia," Tom said. "They are not yucky. They are sweet and soft. And they make you powerful. Look, I can lift this chair with one hand!"

Tom lifted the chair with one hand. He showed Mia. Mia was surprised. She wondered if beans really made Tom powerful. She looked at her plate. She saw a small bean. She picked it up. She looked at it. She smelled it. She put it in her mouth. She chewed it. She tasted it.

Mia smiled. The bean was not yucky. It was yummy. It was sweet and soft. She liked it. She ate another bean. And another. And another. She ate all her beans. She felt good. She felt strong. She felt powerful.

"Mom, look, I ate all my beans!" Mia said. "Can I lift the chair too?"

Mom smiled. She was proud of Mia. She said yes. Mia lifted the chair with one hand. She showed Mom and Tom. They clapped for her.

"See, Mia, beans are good for you," Mom said. "They make you strong and powerful. And they make you happy."

Mia nodded. She was happy. She liked beans. She hugged Mom and Tom. They hugged her back. They ate their bread. They drank their milk. They had a good lunch. They thanked Mom. They said beans were their favorite food.

Lily was impatient. She wanted to go outside and play with her ball. But Mom said no. It was raining hard. There was a big shower from the sky. Lily looked out the window and saw the water falling on the grass and the flowers.

"Mom, when will the shower stop?" Lily asked.

"Soon, I hope. But we have to wait until it is safe and dry," Mom said.

Lily sighed. She was bored. She did not like to wait. She looked around the room. She saw her teddy bear on the couch. She had an idea. She ran to the couch and grabbed her teddy bear. She also took a blanket from the closet.

"Mom, look what I am doing!" Lily said.

Mom turned and saw Lily. Lily had covered her teddy bear with the blanket. She had made a tent for him. She was pretending that he was hiding from the shower.

"That's very clever, Lily. You are making your teddy bear cozy and warm," Mom said.

Lily smiled. She was happy. She liked to play with her teddy bear. She crawled under the blanket with him. She gave him a hug and a kiss.

"Maybe the shower will stop soon. Then we can go outside and play with the ball. But for now, we can have fun in our tent," Lily said to her teddy bear.

The end.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She made many pictures of her family, her friends, and her toys. She was very creative and used many colors. She hung her pictures on the wall with tape.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, I want to teach you how to write your name. It is easy and fun. You can use your crayons or a pencil." Lily was excited. She wanted to learn how to write her name.

Her mom gave her a piece of paper and a pencil. She showed her how to make the letters L, I, L, and Y. She said, "This is how you write Lily. You can copy me or make your own letters. Try it, Lily."

Lily tried to write her name. She made a big L, a small i, a big L, and a small y. She was proud of her name. She showed it to her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "Good job, Lily. You are a smart girl. You can write your name."

Lily wanted to write her name again. She took another piece of paper and a crayon. She wrote her name in red. Then she wrote it in blue. Then she wrote it in green. She filled the paper with her name in different colors. She was happy.

She showed her paper to her mom. Her mom said, "Wow, Lily. You are very creative. You made a beautiful rainbow of your name. I love it."

Lily said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are a good teach."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a good learn. Now, let's wipe the table and put away the crayons and papers. Then we can have a snack."

Tom and Lily wanted to help Mom make a cake. Mom said they could stir the batter in a big bowl. She gave them a spoon and a belt. She said the belt was to tie their aprons. She went to get some eggs from the fridge.

Tom and Lily put on their aprons and tied them with the belt. They took turns to stir the batter. It was thick and sticky. They liked how it smelled. They wondered how it would taste. Lily had an idea. She said to Tom, "Let's try some batter. Mom won't know."

Tom was not sure. He said, "Mom said not to eat the batter. It might make us sick." But Lily said, "Just a little bit. It won't hurt." She dipped her finger in the bowl and licked it. She said, "Mmm, it's yummy. You try too."

Tom looked at the bowl. He wanted to taste the batter. He thought Mom would not mind. He dipped his finger in the bowl and licked it. He said, "You're right. It's yummy." They smiled at each other. They dipped their fingers again and again. They ate a lot of batter.

Then they heard Mom coming back. They quickly put the spoon in the bowl and wiped their fingers. They pretended to stir the batter. Mom came in and said, "Good job, kids. You stirred the batter very well. Now let's put it in the pan and bake it."

She poured the batter in the pan. She noticed it was not very full. She said, "That's strange. I thought I made enough batter. Did you eat some of it?" Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt guilty. They did not say anything. Mom saw their faces. She said, "I see. You ate some of the batter. That was not very nice. You should have waited for the cake. Now we won't have enough for everyone. And you might get a tummy ache."

Tom and Lily felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We won't do it again. We just wanted to taste it. It was yummy." Mom said, "I know, but you have to be patient and follow the rules. Next time, ask me first. And don't eat raw batter. It's not good for you. Now go wash your hands and face. And don't touch the oven. It's hot."

Tom and Lily did what Mom said. They washed their hands and face. They did not touch the oven. They smelled the cake baking. It smelled even yummier than the batter. They hoped Mom would forgive them. They hoped they would not get a tummy ache. They hoped there would be enough cake for everyone. They learned their lesson. They would not eat the batter again.

Anna and Ben are playing in the garden. They see a big apple tree with red apples. They want to eat some apples, but they have to ask Mom first.

"Mom, can we have some apples?" Anna calls.

"Yes, you can, but only one each. And wash them first, please," Mom says.

Anna and Ben run to the apple tree. They pick two apples, one for each. They are very yummy. They bite and chew and smile.

But then they see a big dog. The dog is barking and running to them. He wants their apples. Anna and Ben are scared.

"Quick, hide!" Ben says.

They run behind a bush. They hold their apples tight. They hope the dog will not find them.

The dog sniffs and searches. He cannot see them, but he can smell them. He comes closer and closer to the bush.

Anna and Ben are very quiet. They do not want the dog to hear them.

But then Anna sneezes. Achoo!

The dog hears the sneeze. He jumps to the bush. He sees Anna and Ben and their apples.

"Roof, roof!" he barks.

Anna and Ben scream. They drop their apples and run to Mom.

"Mom, help! The dog wants our apples!" they cry.

Mom comes out. She sees the dog. She knows the dog. He is their neighbor's dog. He is friendly, but he likes apples too.

"Bad dog, go home!" Mom says.

The dog looks at Mom. He looks at the apples. He picks one apple and runs away.

Mom hugs Anna and Ben. She is not angry. She is glad they are safe.

"Are you OK, my loves?" she asks.

"Yes, Mom, we are OK. But we lost our apples," Anna says.

"That's OK, we have more apples. Come on, let's go inside and wash them. And maybe we can share one with the dog next time. He is not a bad dog, he is just hungry," Mom says.

Anna and Ben nod. They follow Mom inside. They still like apples. They are still yummy. But they do not like to hide from dogs. They like to play in the garden.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to help Mom in the kitchen. Mom is making a cake for Dad's birthday. She gives Lily and Ben some jobs.

Lily gets to zip the eggs. She cracks them on the edge of a bowl and opens them. She pours the yellow stuff inside the bowl. She likes to see it splash. She takes a fork and stirs it fast. She makes bubbles in the egg.

Ben gets to grease the pan. He takes a paper and some butter. He rubs the butter on the paper. He wipes the paper on the pan. He covers the pan with butter. He likes to feel it slide. He makes sure there is no dry spot on the pan.

Mom mixes the flour, the sugar, the milk and the egg in a big bowl. She adds some vanilla. She says it makes the cake sweet. She pours the batter in the pan. She puts the pan in the oven. She sets the timer.

Lily and Ben wait for the cake to bake. They smell the sweet vanilla. They hear the timer beep. Mom takes the pan out of the oven. She lets it cool on the rack.

"Can we have some cake now?" Lily asks.

"Not yet, sweetie. We have to wait for Dad to come home. Then we can surprise him with the cake and sing happy birthday." Mom says.

"Okay, Mom. We will wait. But can we lick the bowl?" Ben asks.

"Sure, you can lick the bowl. But don't eat too much. You don't want to spoil your appetite." Mom says.

Lily and Ben take the bowl and the fork. They lick the sweet batter. They smile at each other. They love to help Mom in the kitchen.

Sara and Tom were going to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings and slide and see the ducks. But when they got to the car, mom said they had to delay. She had to make a phone call to an old friend.

"Who is your old friend, mom?" Sara asked.

"Her name is Anna. She was my friend when I was little like you. She is elderly now and lives far away. She needs to talk to me about something important," mom said.

"Can we talk to her too?" Tom asked.

"Maybe later, sweetie. She is not feeling well and needs some quiet. But you can say hello to her when I finish," mom said.

Sara and Tom were bored. They wanted to go to the park. They looked at the books and toys in the car, but they did not want to play with them. They looked out the window and saw the sun and the clouds and the birds, but they did not want to watch them. They looked at each other and sighed.

"Mom, how long will you delay?" Sara asked.

"Just a few more minutes, honey. I know you are eager to go to the park, but sometimes we have to be patient and kind to our old friends. They need our love and support, especially when they are elderly and sick," mom said.

Sara and Tom nodded. They understood. They loved their mom and they wanted her to be happy. They also wanted to be nice to her old friend Anna. They decided to wait quietly and give mom some time. They hoped Anna would feel better soon. They also hoped they would still have some time to go to the park and play.

Anna liked to examine things. She liked to look at them very closely and touch them and smell them and sometimes taste them. She examined her toys, her books, her clothes, and anything else she could find.

One day, she decided to examine the bathtub. She climbed on a stool and looked inside. It was an ordinary bathtub, white and shiny, with a faucet and a drain and a plug. She turned the faucet and water came out. She put her hand under the water and felt it was warm. She smiled and turned the faucet more.

She examined the plug. It was a rubber duck with a hole in its mouth. She pulled it out and water started to go down the drain. She put it back and water stopped. She pulled it out and put it back again and again. She giggled and said, "Quack, quack, quack!"

She examined the drain. It was a metal circle with holes in it. She wondered what was behind it. She stuck her finger in one of the holes and felt something slimy. She pulled her finger out and saw a hair. She made a face and said, "Yuck!"

She heard her mom call her name. She turned and saw her mom standing in the door. Her mom looked at the bathtub and saw it was full of water. She looked at Anna and saw she was wet and soapy. She said, "Anna, what are you doing?"

Anna said, "I'm examining the bathtub, Mom. It's very interesting."

Her mom said, "I'm sure it is, but it's also very messy. Come on, let's get you dry and clean. And next time, please ask me before you examine the bathtub, okay?"

Anna said, "Okay, Mom. But can I examine something else later?"

Her mom said, "Maybe, but only if it's not too messy or dangerous. And only with my permission. Now, let's go." She took Anna's hand and led her to the towel. Anna hugged her mom and said, "I love you, Mom."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Anna. You're a very curious and smart girl. But sometimes you need to be more careful and listen to me." She wrapped Anna in the towel and dried her off. She kissed her on the head and said, "Now, let's go and find something else to examine. Something more ordinary and less wet."

Dad came over and checked the bike. He saw the screw and tried to tighten it. But it was too hard. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can take your bike to the mechanic. He can fix it for you."

"Who is the mechanic?" Lily asked.

"The mechanic is a person who knows how to fix bikes and cars and other things that move. He has a lot of tools and parts. He is very nice and harmless. He won't hurt your bike. He will make it work again."

Lily nodded. She trusted her dad. She got off her bike and walked with him to the car. They put the bike in the trunk and drove to the mechanic's shop. There, they met the mechanic. He was a big man with a blue shirt and a cap. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, little girl. What's wrong with your bike?"

Lily pointed at the wheel and said, "It goes clank-clank-clank. It has a loose screw."

The mechanic looked at the bike and said, "Ah, I see. That's an easy fix. I just need to replace the screw with a new one. It will only take a few minutes. You can wait here and watch me if you want."

Lily nodded. She was curious. She followed the mechanic to his workbench. She saw him take out a new screw and a screwdriver. He unscrewed the old screw and threw it in a bin. He screwed the new screw in the wheel. He spun the wheel and it was quiet. He said, "There, it's done. Your bike is good as new. You can try it now."

Lily was happy. She thanked the mechanic and gave him a hug. She took her bike and rode it around the shop. It was smooth and fast and had no noise. She rang the bell and said, "I love my bike. Thank you, mechanic. Thank you, dad."

Dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you're happy. Now, let's return to the park and have some fun."

One day, a jolly alligator went for a walk in the swamp. He liked to splash in the water and look for fish to eat. He saw a big frog sitting on a log and decided to say hello.

"Hello, frog," said the alligator. "Do you want to play with me?"

The frog was scared of the alligator and his big teeth. He did not want to play with him. He wanted to hop away. But he was polite and said, "What do you want to play, alligator?"

The alligator thought for a moment and said, "Let's play clap. I clap my hands and you clap your feet. Then we take turns and see who can clap faster and louder."

The frog did not like this game. He knew that the alligator had big hands and he had small feet. He knew that the alligator could clap faster and louder than him. He thought that the alligator wanted to trick him and eat him. But he was polite and said, "OK, alligator, let's play clap."

The alligator was happy and said, "Good, frog, let's start. I go first." He clapped his hands together with a loud snap. The frog jumped in fear and clapped his feet together with a soft tap. The alligator said, "Your turn, frog. Clap faster and louder."

The frog did not want to clap faster and louder. He wanted to hop away. But he was polite and said, "OK, alligator, I try." He clapped his feet together with a little more force. The alligator said, "My turn, alligator. Clap faster and louder."

The alligator clapped his hands together with a louder snap. The frog jumped higher and clapped his feet together with a little more noise. The alligator said, "Your turn, frog. Clap faster and louder."

The frog did not want to clap faster and louder. He wanted to hop away. But he was polite and said, "OK, alligator, I try." He clapped his feet together with all his strength. The alligator said, "My turn, alligator. Clap faster and louder."

The alligator clapped his hands together with the loudest snap. The frog jumped so high that he flew off the log and landed on another log far away. The alligator said, "Where did you go, frog? Come back and play clap with me."

But the frog did not come back. He was glad that he escaped from the alligator. He said to himself, "I do not want to play clap with the alligator. He is not jolly. He is scary. I will play with my friends who are nice and fun."

The end.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes we make mistakes and hurt others, but we can say sorry and make up for it. We can also share what we have and be kind to others. We can make new friends and have more fun.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to chase it.

One time, the ball rolled under the fence and into the street. Tim and Mia ran to the fence and looked for the ball. They saw it on the other side, near a big car. Tim wanted to get the ball back. He said to Mia, "I can go under the fence and get the ball. You stay here and watch."

Mia said, "No, Tim, don't go. The street is dangerous. There are many cars and they go fast. You can get hurt. We can ask a grown-up to help us."

But Tim did not listen to Mia. He said, "I am not afraid. I am fast. I can escape the cars. You are a baby. You are scared." He crawled under the fence and ran to the ball.

Mia was worried. She shouted, "Tim, come back. Please, come back." She saw a bright light coming from the car. It was the sun reflecting on the window. She blinked her eyes and rubbed them. She could not see Tim or the ball.

She heard a loud honk and a screech. She heard Tim scream. She felt a cold sweat on her forehead. She cried, "Tim, Tim, are you okay?"

She saw a man get out of the car. He ran to Tim and picked him up. He said, "Don't worry, kid, you are okay. You just have a scratch on your knee. But you were very lucky. You could have been hit by the car. Why did you run into the street? Where is your mom or dad?"

Tim said, "I wanted to get my ball. It was under the fence. I thought I could escape the cars. I am sorry. I was wrong. I should have listened to Mia. She told me not to go. She was right. The street is dangerous."

The man said, "Yes, she was right. And you should be sorry. You were very foolish and reckless. You should always listen to your friends when they care about you. And you should never play near the street. It is not a place for kids. It is a place for cars. Do you understand?"

Tim said, "Yes, I understand. I am sorry, Mia. I am sorry, mister. I will never do that again. I will always listen to Mia. She is my friend. She is not a baby. She is smart."

Mia said, "It's okay, Tim. I am glad you are okay. I am your friend. I love you. But don't ever scare me like that again. Promise?"

Tim said, "I promise. I love you too. Can we have our ball back, please?"

The man said, "Sure, here you go. But be careful. And have fun. And remember, the street is not a place for kids. It is a place for cars."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their friends when they care about them, to avoid playing near the street, and to be careful of the dangers of cars.

Mom hugged Lily and Max and said, "Let's go and see the cactus. Maybe we can do something to help it. Maybe we can give it some sun and some air. Maybe we can sing to it and make it happy."

Lily and Max agreed. They followed Mom to the garden. They saw the cactus. It was still brown and swollen, but it had a tiny flower on top. It was a sign of hope.

Lily and Max smiled. They said, "Look, Mom. The cactus has a flower. It is not dead. It is alive. It is beautiful."

Mom smiled too. She said, "Yes, it is. The cactus is strong. It can survive. It can grow. It can bloom. Just like you, my kids. You are strong. You can survive. You can grow. You can bloom. You are beautiful."

They hugged the cactus gently and said, "We love you, cactus. We are sorry, cactus. We are happy, cactus."

The cactus felt their love and their sorry and their happy. It felt better. It soaked up their warmth and their kindness. It thanked them with its flower.

The end.

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood.

"Can we still be friends with the owl, mom?" Ben said.

"Maybe, but you have to be gentle and quiet. And don't touch him again. He likes his space," mom said.

Ben and Lily agreed. They waved goodbye to the owl. The owl waved back.

"Bye, bye, owl. See you next time," Ben and Lily said.

The owl said, "Who? Who?"

"Let's go surf!" Tom said. He grabbed his bucket and ran to the water.

"Wait, Tom!" Lily said. She remembered what Mom had told them. "Mom said to be careful. The waves are too big for us. They can knock us down and hurt us. We should stay close to the sand."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He thought he was brave and strong. He wanted to surf like the big kids. He jumped into the water and tried to balance on his bucket. He felt the wind and the spray. He smiled and shouted, "Whee!"

But then a big wave came. It was bigger than Tom. It lifted him up and threw him down. Tom lost his bucket and his balance. He went under the water. He felt scared and cold. He could not breathe. He cried for help.

Lily saw what happened. She was worried about Tom. She ran to the water and looked for him. She saw his head pop up. He was coughing and splashing. She reached out her hand and pulled him to the shore. She hugged him and said, "Are you okay, Tom?"

Tom was not okay. He was wet and shivering. He was also embarrassed. He had been silly and foolish. He had not listened to Lily and Mom. He had put himself in danger. He felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You were right. I should have listened to you. You warned me, but I did not listen. I was stupid. Thank you for saving me."

Lily was glad that Tom was safe. She was also kind and forgiving. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm happy you're okay. You're not stupid. You just made a mistake. We all make mistakes sometimes. But we have to learn from them. Next time, we should listen to Mom and be careful. Okay?"

Tom nodded. He said, "Okay. Next time, I will listen to you and Mom. And I will not try to surf on a bucket. That was dumb."

Lily smiled. She said, "That's good, Tom. Come on, let's go back to the sand. We can build a sandcastle instead. That's more fun and safer than surfing."

Tom agreed. He said, "Yes, let's do that. And maybe we can find my bucket. I hope the wave did not take it away."

They held hands and walked back to the sand. They were happy to be together. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and to listen to warnings. They also learned to be kind and forgiving. They were good siblings and good friends.

As she sat in the grass, Lily noticed how quiet it was. She liked the silence because she could hear the birds singing and the leaves rustling in the breeze. Suddenly, her little brother came running outside and started making a lot of noise. Lily didn't like the noise because it interrupted the peaceful silence.

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her what she did outside. Lily told her about the green butterfly and how she loved the silence. Her mom smiled and said she valued those things too. From then on, Lily made sure to appreciate the beauty of nature and the importance of silence.

Tom and Jerry looked at the toy bird and forgot about their quarrel. They started to play together, chasing the toy bird around the house. Suddenly, Jerry saw a flea on his fur and started to scratch himself.

"Look, Tom! I have a flea on me!" said Jerry.

"Don't worry, Jerry. I will help you get rid of it," said Tom, licking Jerry's fur to get rid of the flea.

And they lived happily ever after, playing together and being friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little train with a coal car. Every day, the train would move along the tracks carrying coal to its destination. One day, the train needed to move faster than usual. The engine roared louder and louder as it raced along the track.

The coal car rattled and shook, with coal spilling everywhere. Suddenly, the train came to a stop. The engine was too hot. But then a funny thing happened. One of the coal pieces started to move. It scuttled around in the coal car, bumping into the other chunks of coal. 

The train started up again. This time, the coal piece danced and moved a bit faster, so it was easier for the train to move. Everywhere it went, the coal piece was so loud that it even made the engine take notice.

The train and the coal piece travelled many miles together. It was a friendship like no other until the train eventually reached its destination and the coal piece said goodbye. 

And that's the story of how a little coal piece helped the train move faster!

The white rabbit said goodbye and disappeared back into the garden, but the little girl and her sister knew they would never forget their magical day. They talked about it all the way back home, and the little girl knew she was lucky to have such a big, adventurous sister.

Lily realized that hiding in the night was not a good idea. She went back to her friends and they all laughed at her silly hiding spot. From then on, Lily decided to only hide in places where she felt safe and could be found easily.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and wanted something hot to eat. He went to his mom and said, "Mommy, I'm hungry. Can you provide me some food?"

His mom replied, "Sure, Timmy. What would you like to eat?"

"I want some hot soup," Timmy said.

But his mom said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. We don't have any soup. How about a sandwich instead?"

Timmy didn't want a sandwich. He wanted soup. He started to cry and said, "But I'm so hungry, and I really want some hot soup."

His mom felt bad for Timmy and said, "Okay, I'll make you some soup. But next time, please don't cry. Just tell me what you want, and I'll try to provide it for you."

Lily's parents realized that they had accidentally packed the wrong medication for her brother's asthma. They were worried and didn't know what to do. The campsite was also very noisy, which made it hard to think. But then, Lily had an idea. She remembered that they had passed a pharmacy on the way to the campsite. So, they quickly packed up their things and drove to the pharmacy to get the right medication for her brother. They were able to get the medication and returned to the campsite, where Lily's brother was able to breathe easier and everyone could finally relax and enjoy the rest of their camping trip.

Benny nibbled on the root and it tasted delicious! "Thank you, Mr. Owl," Benny said. "I never knew roots could be so yummy."

"You're welcome, Benny," said the owl. "Just be careful not to eat any harmful roots. Always ask someone wise before you eat something you don't know." 

Benny nodded and hopped away, feeling happy and full. From that day on, he always asked for advice before trying new things.

One day, a young rabbit named Lily wanted to play with her friends in the meadow. She was very bored in her burrow and wished for some fun. She asked her mother if she could go out.

"Be careful, Lily," her mother said. "There are many dangers in the meadow. You have to watch out for the fox, the hawk, and the farmer. They are all very hungry and want to catch you."

"I know, mother," Lily said. "But I have a plan. I will stay close to the bushes and the rocks. I will run fast and hide if I see anything scary. And I will be back before dark."

"Alright, Lily," her mother said. "But promise me you will be careful."

Lily promised and hopped out of the burrow. She was very happy to see her friends waiting for her. They greeted her with joy and started to play. They chased each other, nibbled on the grass, and rolled in the dirt. They had a lot of fun.

But Lily did not notice that a fox was watching them from behind a tree. He licked his lips and thought, "What a tasty snack. I will wait for the right moment and pounce on that young rabbit. She looks so juicy and tender."

He crept closer and closer, until he was ready to attack. He jumped out of his hiding place and ran towards Lily. She saw him and screamed. She ran as fast as she could, but the fox was faster. He was about to catch her, when suddenly, a loud bang echoed in the air. The fox stopped and looked up. He saw the farmer with a gun, aiming at him. He realized he had fallen into a trap. He turned around and ran away, as fast as he could.

Lily was safe. She thanked the farmer, who smiled and waved at her. She ran back to her friends, who hugged her and cheered. She was very glad that her plan had worked. She had stayed close to the bushes and the rocks, where the farmer had set up his trap. She had run fast and hidden behind a rock, where the farmer had seen her and scared away the fox. She told her mother everything that had happened. Her mother was very proud of her and hugged her. She said, "You are a very brave and smart rabbit, Lily. "Hey, give them back. They are ours," Sara and Ben shout.

"What is wrong, Sara and Ben?" she asks.

"A big boy took our shapes. We were arguing. We did not share," Sara and Ben say.

The teacher nods. She has an idea.

She takes out a long rope. She makes a circle with it. She puts it on the floor.

"Look, this is a big circle. It has no corners. It is round," she says.

She takes out a long stick. She makes a square with it. She puts it on the floor.

"Look, this is a big square. It has four corners. It is strong," she says.

She smiles. She says, "You can both play with the circle and the square. They are different, but they are both good. You can learn from each other. You can have fun together. You can be friends."

Sara and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They nod.

They say, "Thank you, teacher. You are right. We can share. We can be friends."

They hug. They play with the circle and the square. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. We can respect and appreciate our differences. We can be friends.

She runs downstairs and finds her mom in the kitchen. She says, "Look, mom, I'm a clown!" She makes a silly face and honks a horn. Her mom smiles and says, "You look very funny, Lisa. You are a great clown."

She runs to the living room and finds her dad on the couch. He is sad. He had a bad day at work. He does not want to laugh. Lisa says, "Look, dad, I'm a clown!" She makes a silly face and honks a horn. Her dad does not smile. He says, "Not now, Lisa. I'm not in the mood for jokes."

Lisa feels sad. She does not want to make her dad sad. She loves her dad. She is compassionate. She thinks of a way to cheer him up. She says, "I'm sorry, dad. I just wanted to make you happy. Can I give you a hug?" She takes off her red nose and her wig and hugs her dad.

Her dad feels her hug and her love. He hugs her back and says, "Thank you, Lisa. You are very sweet. You make me happy. I love you." He smiles and says, "You know what? You are a great clown. And a great daughter." He makes a silly face and honks a horn. Lisa laughs and says, "I love you, too, dad. You are a great dad. And a great clown." They laugh together and hug again.

She put on the dress and the shoes and wrapped the tie around her neck. She looked at herself in the mirror and smiled. She thought she matched very well. She felt very happy and proud. She wanted to show her mom how she looked.

She ran downstairs to find her mom, who was in the kitchen. She called out, "Mom, mom, look at me! I'm a princess!" Her mom turned around and saw her. She was surprised and amused. She said, "Wow, Lily, you look very nice. But where did you get that tie?"

Lily pointed to the closet and said, "From the box. It's very pretty, right? It matches my dress and shoes." Her mom nodded and said, "Yes, it is very pretty, but it's also very expensive. It's a special tie that your dad gave me for our anniversary. It's not for playing, it's for keeping."

Lily felt sad and confused. She didn't know it was a special tie. She thought it was just a fun tie. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. I just wanted to look like a princess." It was angry and frustrated. It roared and stomped. It woke up Lily and Tom. They heard the noise and got scared. They jumped out of their beds and ran to Mom and Dad.

"Mom, Dad, there's a bear outside!" Lily and Tom cried.

Mom and Dad woke up and heard the bear too. They grabbed their phones and called for help. They told Lily and Tom to stay calm and quiet. They waited for the ranger to come.

The ranger came and scared the bear away. He checked the car and the cabin and made sure everyone was safe. He told Mom and Dad to lock their luggage inside and to keep their food in a metal box. He told Lily and Tom to never feed or approach a bear. He said they were lucky the bear did not break into the cabin.

Lily and Tom learned their lesson. They thanked the ranger and hugged Mom and Dad. They went back to their beds and tried to sleep. They did not dream of bears anymore. They dreamed of going home.

Lily liked to pick flowers from the garden. She thought they were pretty and smelled good. She wanted to make a bouquet for her mom. But mom said, "No, Lily, you cannot pick the flowers. They are not for you. They are for the bees and the birds and the butterflies. They need the flowers to live and be happy. If you pick the flowers, you will hurt them and make them sad. You can look at the flowers, but you cannot touch them."

Lily was sad. She did not want to hurt the bees and the birds and the butterflies. But she also wanted to make her mom happy. She thought, maybe I can pick just one flower. Mom will not notice. And one flower will not make a big difference. So she waited until mom was busy in the kitchen. Then she sneaked into the garden and looked for a flower to pick. She saw a big, red, shiny flower. It was the most beautiful flower she had ever seen. She reached out her hand to pick it.

But then she heard a buzzing sound. It was a bee. The bee was flying around the flower. The bee saw Lily and said, "Stop, Lily, stop! Do not pick that flower. That is my flower. I need that flower to make honey. Honey is my food. If you pick that flower, I will have no food. I will be hungry and sick. Please, Lily, leave that flower alone."

Lily was surprised. She did not know that the bee could talk. She did not know that the flower was his food. She felt sorry for the bee. She said, "I'm sorry, bee. I did not know that. I will not pick your flower. I will find another flower."

But then she heard a chirping sound. It was a bird. The bird was sitting on a branch above the flower. The bird saw Lily and said, "Stop, Lily, stop! Do not pick any flower. All the flowers are my friends. They make me happy and sing. If you pick any flower, you will make me sad and quiet. Please, Lily, leave the flowers alone."

Lily was amazed. She did not know that the bird could talk. She did not know that the flowers were his friends. She felt sorry for the bird. She said, "I'm sorry, bird. I did not know that. I will not pick any flower. I will find something else."

But then she heard a fluttering sound. It was a butterfly. The butterfly was flying around the flowers. The butterfly saw Lily and said, "Stop, Lily, stop! Do not pick anything. Everything in the garden is beautiful and special. If you pick anything, you will make the garden less beautiful and less special. Please, Lily, enjoy the garden as it is."

Lily was stunned. She did not know that the butterfly could talk. She did not know that everything in the garden was beautiful and special. She felt sorry for the butterfly. She said, "I'm sorry, butterfly. I did not know that. I will not pick anything. I will enjoy the garden as it is."

Then she heard a voice behind her. It was her mom. Mom had seen everything. Mom said, "Lily, I'm proud of you. You listened to the bee and the bird and the butterfly. You learned that the garden is not for you to pick. It is for you to share and respect. You did the right thing. You are a good girl."

Lily smiled. She hugged her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love the garden. And I love the bee and the bird and the butterfly. They are my friends too."

Mom smiled. She hugged Lily. She said, "I love you too, Lily. And I have a surprise for you. Come with me."

Mom took Lily to the kitchen. There, on the table, was a bouquet of flowers. They were not from the garden. They were from the store. Mom said, "These are for you, Lily. You can pick these flowers. They are not ordinary flowers. They are special flowers. They are for you to keep and enjoy. They are a reward for being kind and wise."

Lily was happy. She thanked her mom. She took the bouquet of flowers. They were pretty and smelled good. She said, "These are the best flowers ever. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever."

The end.

Sam was a pupil in the big school. He liked to learn new things and play with his friends. But he did not like his teacher, Mr. Fox. Mr. Fox was harsh and mean. He always shouted at the pupils and gave them hard work.

One day, Mr. Fox told the pupils to write a story. He said he would read the best story to the whole school and everyone would applaud. Sam tried his best to write a good story. He wrote about a brave knight who fought a dragon and saved a princess. He was proud of his story.

When Mr. Fox collected the stories, he looked at Sam's story and frowned. He said, "This story is silly and bad. You have no talent for writing. You should be ashamed of yourself." He tore Sam's story into pieces and threw it in the bin. Sam felt sad and angry. He wanted to cry, but he did not.

The next day, Mr. Fox read the best story to the whole school. It was his own story. He wrote about how he was a smart and handsome teacher who taught the best pupils in the world. He said, "This story is brilliant and true. You should all admire me and learn from me." He smiled and waited for everyone to applaud.

But no one applauded. The pupils looked bored and annoyed. They did not like Mr. Fox's story. They thought it was boring and false. They whispered to each other, "This story is silly and bad. He has no talent for writing. He should be ashamed of himself." They laughed and booed. Mr. Fox felt sad and angry. He wanted to cry, but he did not. He ran away from the school and never came back.

Sam was happy. He did not care about his torn story. He knew he had a good imagination and a good heart. He said to his friends, "Let's write our own stories and share them with each other. We don't need Mr. Fox to tell us what to write." His friends agreed and applauded. They wrote their own stories and had fun. They learned to be kind and creative. They were the best pupils in the world.

Lily and Sam went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. Lily liked the lions best. She wanted to pet them, but Mom said no. Sam liked the monkeys best. He laughed when they jumped and played.

The zoo keeper came to feed the snake. He opened the box and put a mouse inside. The snake saw the mouse and moved fast. It wrapped around the mouse and squeezed it. Then it opened its mouth and swallowed it whole. Lily and Sam watched with wide eyes.

"Wow, that was cool!" Sam said.

"Yuck, that was gross!" Lily said.

The zoo keeper closed the box and locked it. He smiled at Lily and Sam.

"Hello, kids. Do you like the snake?" he asked.

Sam nodded. "Yes, it is very strong and smart. What is its name?"

The zoo keeper said, "His name is Ziggy. He is a python. He can eat animals bigger than him. He can also fit in small places. He can curl up and hide."

One day, their mom says, "Ben and Lily, today we are going to do some math. It is good for your brains and it will help you in school. You can use your blocks and cars and dolls to help you."

Ben and Lily groan. They do not want to do math. They want to play. They say, "Mom, please, no math. Math is bad. We do not like math."

Mom smiles. She says, "Math is not bad. Math is fun. You can make patterns and puzzles and games with math. And you can learn new things and increase your skills. Come on, let me show you."

Mom takes Ben and Lily to the table. She gives them some blocks and cars and dolls. She says, "Let's start with some easy math. How many blocks do you have, Ben?"

Ben counts his blocks. He says, "I have four blocks."

Mom says, "Good. Now, if I give you one more block, how many blocks will you have?"

Ben thinks. He says, "I will have five blocks."

Mom says, "That's right. You just did math. You added one block to four blocks and you got five blocks. That is called addition. Can you say addition?"

Ben says, "Addition."

Mom says, "Good. Now, Lily, how many dolls do you have?"

Lily counts her dolls. She says, "I have three dolls."

Mom says, "Good. Now, if I take away one doll, how many dolls will you have?"

Lily thinks. She says, "I will have two dolls."

Mom says, "That's right. You just did math. You took away one doll from three dolls and you got two dolls. That is called subtraction. Can you say subtraction?"

Lily says, "Subtraction."

And the more you increase your math skills, the more you can do with math. Math is amazing. Can you say amazing?"

Ben and Lily say, "Amazing."

Ben and Lily nod. They say, "Yes, let's do that. Math is fun. We like math."

Mom smiles. She says, "I'm glad you like math. Math is good for you. And I'm proud of you. You are smart and clever and wonderful. I love you."

They had come to get the lion and take it back to the zoo. They had a big truck and a cage. They put the lion in the cage and drove away.

Sam and Mia were relieved. They were safe and the lion was safe too. They decided to never touch the object again. They also decided to never pretend to be lions again. They liked to be children. They went back to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run.

"Hey, what is that?" Tim asks. He points at the mark.

"That is nothing," Lily says. She tries to hide the mark with her hand. "It is just a mistake."

"A mistake?" Tim says. He grabs Lily's paper and looks closer. "It is a bug! You drew a bug on your car!"

Lily feels angry and embarrassed. She did not mean to draw a bug. She was trying to draw a flower, but the green crayon slipped from her hand.

"It is not a bug!" Lily says. She tries to get her paper back. "It is a flower!"

Tim does not believe her. He thinks she is lying. He laughs at her.

"A flower? That is a silly flower. It has no petals, no stem, no leaves. It is just a dot. A green dot. A bug!"

"Stop it!" Tim says. He pushes Lily back. He wants to keep the paper. He thinks it is funny. "You can't erase a bug! It is still there!"

Tim and Lily feel ashamed and sorry. They know they did wrong. They look at each other and say sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tim says. "I should not have laughed at your drawing. It is not a bug. It is a flower."

"I'm sorry, Tim," Lily says. "I should not have pushed you and erased your drawing. It is not a mistake. It is a lion."

They show their teacher their drawings and smile. They are proud of their work and their friendship.

"Be careful, Ben," she said. "The hanger is sharp. It can hurt you."

Ben did not listen. He thought the hanger was fun. He pretended it was a sword and made noises.

"Zap! Zap! I am a hero!" he said.

He ran towards Lily and tried to touch her with the hanger. Lily was scared. She did not want to play with the hanger. She moved away from Ben.

"Stop, Ben, stop!" she said. "The hanger is not a toy. It can hurt me."

But Ben did not stop. He was too excited. He swung the hanger faster and faster. He did not see where he was going. He tripped on a rug and fell down. The hanger hit his arm. It made a cut. It was red and wet. It hurt a lot.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben cried. "The hanger hurt me!"

Lily ran to him and saw his arm. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him and said,

"I'm sorry, Ben. I told you the hanger was sharp. It can hurt you."

She helped him get up and took him to their mom. Their mom saw the cut and said,

"Oh, Ben, what happened? Did you play with the hanger?"

Ben nodded and said,

"Yes, mom. I'm sorry. I was silly. The hanger hurt me."

Their mom cleaned the cut and put a band-aid on it. She said,

"It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you're sorry. The hanger is not a toy. It is sharp. It can hurt you and Lily. Next time, listen to Lily. She is a good sister. She cares about you."

Ben said,

"Thank you, mom. I love you. I love Lily too. I will listen to her. I will not play with the hanger again."

Lily smiled and said,

"I love you too, Ben. I'm happy you're okay. Let's play with our toys and books. They are safe and fun."

They hugged each other and went back to their room. They played with their toys and books. They did not touch the hanger. They were happy and careful.
