But they needed a coin to play. They looked in their pockets, but they had no coins. They looked on the ground, but they saw no coins. They looked at each other, but they had no ideas.

Then they saw a man who was walking by. He had a big bag that made a jingle sound. Anna and Ben thought he had many coins in his bag. They ran to the man and asked him, "Please, can you give us a coin? We want to play the fun games."

The man looked at Anna and Ben. He smiled and said, "Sure, I can give you a coin. I have many coins in my bag. I work at the bank and I supply the coins to the machines. But you have to do something for me first."

Anna and Ben were curious. They asked, "What do we have to do?"

The man said, "You have to tell me a joke. If I laugh, I will give you a coin. If I don't laugh, I will keep my coin. Do you want to try?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They liked jokes. They thought hard and tried to remember a funny joke. Anna said, "Why did the chicken cross the road?"

The man said, "I don't know. Why did the chicken cross the road?"

Anna said, "To get to the other slide!"

The man did not laugh. He said, "That is not a joke. That is a fact. Chickens like slides. Try again."

Ben said, "What do you call a fish that wears a bow?"

The man said, "I don't know. What do you call a fish that wears a bow?"

Ben said, "A rainbow!"

The man laughed. He said, "That is a joke. That is funny. I like rainbows. Here is your coin."

He gave Ben a shiny coin. Ben was happy. He said, "Thank you, mister. You are very kind."

Anna was sad. She had no coin. She said, "I'm sorry, mister. I'm sorry I didn't make you laugh. Can I have a coin too?"

The man looked at Anna. He saw her sad face. He felt sorry for her. He said, "OK, I will give you a coin too. But you have to promise me something."

Anna said, "What do I have to promise?"

The man said, "You have to promise to keep practicing your jokes. Jokes are good for the soul. They make people happy. Do you promise?"

Anna said, "I promise. I will practice my jokes. Thank you, mister. You are very nice."

He gave Anna a shiny coin. Anna was happy. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

"Your mask is nice," Sara says. "It is orange like the sun."

"Thank you," Tom says. "Your mask is nice, too. It is blue like the sky."

They smile with their eyes. They cannot see their mouths. But they can hear their voices.

They run and jump and laugh. They have fun. They care for each other. They are good friends. They wear their masks.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. They see a big hill with many rocks and dirt. They want to climb the hill and see what is on top.

"Come on, Lily, let's go up the hill!" Tom says.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. The rocks are rough and hard. They can hurt your hand." Lily says.

They hold hands and start to climb. They step on the rocks and dirt. They see bugs and flowers. They hear birds and wind. They are happy and curious.

They reach the top of the hill. They look around and see many things. They see the park, the trees, the sky, the sun. They see a pond, a bridge, a boat. They see a house, a car, a dog.

"Wow, look at all the things we can see from here!" Tom says.

"Yes, it is very pretty and fun!" Lily says.

They sit on the rocks and enjoy the view. They feel the sun on their face and the wind in their hair. They smile and laugh.

Then, Lily sees something shiny on the ground. She bends down and picks it up. It is a coin. It is round and silver and has a picture on it.

"Look, Tom, I found something!" Lily says.

"What is it, Lily?" Tom asks.

"It is a coin. It is shiny and pretty. It has a picture of a man on it." Lily says.

"Wow, that is cool, Lily! Where did it come from?" Tom asks.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe someone dropped it here. Maybe it is lucky." Lily says.

"Can I see it, Lily?" Tom asks.

"Sure, Tom, here you go." Lily says.

She gives the coin to Tom. He holds it in his hand. He feels the rough edges and the smooth surface. He looks at the picture and the words. He does not know what they mean.

"Thank you, Lily. This is a nice coin. Do you want to keep it?" Tom asks.

"No, Tom, you can have it. It is a gift from me to you. You are my friend." Lily says.

"Thank you, Lily. You are my friend too. You are very kind." Tom says.

They hug and share the coin. They are happy and grateful. They have found a treasure on the hill.

Lila was a humble fairy who lived in a big garden. She liked to help the flowers grow and make friends with the animals. She did not like to show off or be mean to others.

One day, she saw a new fairy in the garden. He was very shiny and loud. He flew around and said, "Look at me! I am the best fairy ever! I can do anything I want!" He made fun of Lila and her friends. He pulled the petals off the flowers and scared the animals.

Lila felt sad and angry. She wanted to tell him to stop, but she was afraid he would hurt her. She hid behind a rose bush and whispered, "Please, go away. You are not nice. You are hurting the garden."

The shiny fairy heard her and flew over. He laughed and said, "Who are you? You are so small and dull. You are a silly fairy. You can't do anything. Watch this!" He waved his wand and made a big firework in the sky.

Lila was scared of the firework. She saw the animals run away and the flowers wilt. She felt a warm tear roll down her cheek. She wished she could do something to stop him.

Then, she heard a voice in her ear. It was the rose bush. It said, "Don't be afraid, Lila. You are a good fairy. You have a special power. You can make things grow with your love. Use your love to make the garden beautiful again."

Lila felt a spark in her heart. She wiped her tear and smiled. She said, "Thank you, rose bush. You are a good friend. I will try." She flew out of the hiding place and faced the shiny fairy. She said, "Stop, please. You are not the best fairy ever. You are a bad fairy. You are hurting the garden. I love the garden. I will make it beautiful again."

She touched the flowers with her hand and they bloomed. She sang to the animals and they came back. She sprinkled some dust on the firework and it turned into rainbows. The garden was happy and bright.

The shiny fairy was shocked. He said, "How did you do that? You are a powerful fairy. You are better than me. I am sorry. I was wrong. Can you teach me how to be a good fairy?"

Lila was humble. She said, "I am not better than you. I am just different. I can teach you how to be a good fairy. You have to be kind and gentle. You have to care for the garden and the animals. You have to share and listen. You have to use your power for good, not for bad."

The shiny fairy nodded. He said, "I will try. Thank you, Lila. You are a brave fairy. You are a good friend." He smiled and hugged her.

Lila was happy. She said, "You are welcome. You are a smart fairy. You are a good friend, too." She smiled and hugged him back.

The end.

Lila and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big toy elephant that could make sounds. They wanted to hear what the elephant sounded like, so they pressed a button on its ear. The elephant made a loud noise like "Prrrrrr!"

"Wow, that's a funny sound!" Lila said. "Can we record it?"

Ben nodded. He had a small machine that could record sounds. He turned it on and held it near the elephant. He pressed another button on the elephant's ear. The elephant made another noise like "Wooo!"

"Ha ha, that's even funnier!" Ben said. "Let's record more sounds!"

They pressed different buttons on the elephant and recorded all the sounds it made. They had a lot of fun listening to the sounds and laughing.

But then, they heard a voice from the other room. It was Lila's mom.

"Lila, Ben, it's time for lunch. Come and wash your hands."

Lila and Ben put down the elephant and the machine and ran to the kitchen. They forgot to turn off the machine.

While they were eating, the machine played back all the sounds they recorded. The elephant sounded like "Prrrrr! Wooo! Mooo! Quack! Meow!"

Lila's mom heard the noises and came to the living room. She saw the elephant and the machine. She was surprised and confused.

"What is this?" she asked. "Who made these sounds?"

Lila and Ben looked at each other. They felt a little guilty.

"We did, mom," Lila said. "We recorded the elephant's sounds. We wanted to hear what it sounded like."

Lila's mom smiled. She was not angry. She was proud.

"That's very original, Lila and Ben," she said. "You are very creative and curious. But you should also be careful with your toys. You should turn off the machine when you are done. And you should ask before you use someone else's toy. This elephant belongs to your cousin. He might not like it if you change his sounds."

Lila and Ben nodded. They understood. They said sorry to Lila's mom and to the elephant. They promised to be more respectful and responsible with their toys. They also thanked Lila's mom for the lunch and the compliment.

They learned that it is good to explore and learn new things, but it is also important to respect and care for others.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny thing under a big tree. They ran to see what it was.

"Look, Tom, it is gold!" Lily said, picking up a small coin.

"Wow, it is so pretty! Where did it come from?" Tom asked, holding another coin.

"Maybe someone lost it. Maybe it is a treasure!" Lily said, excited.

They looked around and saw more coins scattered on the ground. They filled their pockets with the gold and laughed.

But they did not see a man who was watching them from behind the tree. He was angry and mean. He had buried the gold there and he wanted it back. He had been careless and forgot to cover it well.

He came out of his hiding place and shouted at the twins.

"Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my gold! It is mine, not yours!"

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know what to do. They dropped the coins and ran away. They did not want to fight with the man.

They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. They told her what happened and hugged her.

"It is okay, my loves. You did nothing wrong. The man was bad and greedy. He should not have hidden the gold in the park. You are safe now." Mom said, kissing them.

Tom and Lily felt better. They learned a lesson. They did not want to touch things that did not belong to them. They were happy with what they had. They did not need the gold.

Ben and Lily wanted to make lemonade. They had water and sugar, but they needed lemons. They asked their mom if they could go to the store and buy some lemons. Their mom said yes, but they had to be careful and hold hands.

Ben and Lily walked to the store, holding hands. They saw many things on the way: cars, dogs, flowers, birds. They liked to look at them and talk about them. They were happy.

When they got to the store, they saw a big basket of lemons. They were yellow and shiny and smelled good. Ben and Lily each took a lemon and put it in their pocket. They did not pay for them. They thought no one would notice.

They walked back home, holding hands. They did not see the store man running after them. He was angry. He shouted, "Stop! You stole my lemons! Give them back!"

Ben and Lily heard him and got scared. They ran faster. They did not look where they were going. They crossed the street without looking. A car was coming. It honked. It hit them.

Ben and Lily fell down. They dropped their lemons. They felt pain. They felt dizzy. They saw blood. They cried.

The store man caught up with them. He saw what happened. He felt sorry. He called for help. He said, "I'm sorry. I just wanted my lemons back. I didn't mean to make you run."

But it was too late. Ben and Lily were hurt. They did not make lemonade. They did not go home. They did not see their mom. They did not live.

One day, Sara wanted to play with Lily and her bag. She looked for them in her room, but she could not find them. She asked her mom, but her mom did not know. She asked her dad, but her dad did not know. She asked her brother, but her brother did not answer. He was busy playing with his cars.

Sara was sad. She thought she lost Lily and her bag. She went to her brother's room to see if he had them. She saw Lily on his bed, but she did not see the bag. She ran to the bed and grabbed Lily. She was happy to find her.

But then she saw something on the floor. It was the bag, but it was not the same. It was torn and ripped. There were holes and cuts in it. Sara was angry. She knew her brother did it. He was mean. He did not like her dolls. He liked to tear things.

Sara yelled at her brother. She said he was bad. She said he ruined her bag. She said he had to give her a new one. Her brother did not care. He said the bag was old and ugly. He said it was not tough. He said it was easy to tear. He said he did not want it.

Sara cried. She loved her bag. She did not want a new one. She wanted her old one. She hugged Lily and the bag. She wished they were not torn. She wished her brother was nice. She wished he did not tear things.

Lily was fearful of the rod. She thought Tom might hit her or break something. She backed away and hid behind a box.

"Tom, stop it! You're scaring me!" she cried.

Tom did not listen. He ran after Lily with the rod. He thought it was fun to chase her.

But he did not see the rake that was lying on the ground. He tripped over it and fell. The rod flew out of his hand and hit the window. The window cracked and made a loud noise.

Mommy heard the noise and came out. She saw the broken window, the rod, the rake, and the toys. She was very angry.

"Tom! Lily! What have you done?" she yelled. "You were supposed to clean, not make more trouble!"

Tim and Jen catch up with the dog. They see the cap on the grass. They pick it up.

"Wow!" Sam said. "This is amazing!"

They ran to the beach and had fun. They built sandcastles and collected seashells and splashed in the water. They laughed and sang and forgot about everything else.

But they forgot something. They forgot to tie the rope to the boat. The rope slipped from their hands and went into the water. The anchor went with it. The boat started to move with the wind. Lily and Ben were scared. They shouted for their dad.

Sue shakes her head. She likes grapes too. She does not want to trade. She says to Tom, "No, this is my grape. You eat your carrot."

Tom gets mad. He reaches over and pokes Sue's grape with his finger. He says, "Now your grape is dirty. You have to give it to me."

Sue gets mad too. She pokes Tom's carrot with her finger. She says, "Now your carrot is dirty. You have to give it to me."

They both poke each other's food. They make a mess. The food falls off the plate. The plate is dirty. Mom sees them. She is not happy. She says, "Stop poking each other's food. That is not nice. You have to eat what you have. And you have to clean the plate."

Tom and Lily say they are sorry. They learn to respect the bees and the hive. They do not squeeze the hive again. They play with other things in the garden. They are happy.

"Let me try," Ben said. He pushed and pulled, but nothing happened. He felt frustrated.

"Maybe we can ask Dad for help," Lily said. She was smarter than Ben.

"No, I can do it by myself," Ben said. He was stubborn and proud.

He pushed harder and harder, until he fell over and hit his head. He started to cry.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. She felt sorry for him.

"Are you okay, Ben?" she asked.

"It hurts," Ben said. He was sad and angry.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Maybe we can play something else," Lily said. She wanted to cheer him up.

She looked around and saw a skipping rope. She had an idea.

"Look, Ben, a skipping rope! Do you want to try?" she asked.

Ben wiped his tears and nodded. He liked to try new things.

Lily showed him how to hold the rope and swing it over his head. Then she jumped over it as it touched the ground.

"Your turn, Ben," she said.

Ben took the rope and tried to copy Lily. But he was not good at skipping. He tripped over the rope and fell again.

He felt frustrated again.

"I can't do it, Lily. It's too hard," he said.

Lily helped him up and smiled.

"It's okay, Ben. You just need to practice. Here, let me show you a trick. Hold the rope around your waist, like this. Then swing it from side to side, like this. It's easier and fun," she said.

Ben did as Lily said. He held the rope around his waist and swung it from side to side. He felt the rope tickle his belly and make him laugh.

He liked it.

"Wow, this is fun, Lily. Thank you for showing me," he said.

Lily laughed too.

"You're welcome, Ben. I'm glad you like it. You see, sometimes you need to ask for help or try something different. You don't have to do everything by yourself. We can have more fun together," she said.

Ben nodded.

"You're right, Lily. You're a good sister. I'm sorry for being stubborn and proud. Can we share the box too?" he asked.

Lily nodded.

"Of course, Ben. You're a good brother. Maybe we can find something inside that we both like. Come on, let's go ask Dad for help," she said.

They held hands and ran to the house, leaving the rope behind. They were happy and curious.

The moral of the story is: Don't be stubborn and proud. Ask for help or try something different. You can have more fun with others.

Tim looked around and saw a big tree. He said, "Guess, Sam! What animal lives in a tree?" Sam looked up at the tree and thought for a moment. Then, Sam meowed and pointed at a bird. "Yes, Sam! It's a bird!" Tim clapped and smiled.

The animals didn't know what to do. Then, a wise owl suggested they all march together and show the fox that sharing is better than being greedy. So, they all marched towards the fox's den.

When they got there, the fox was surprised to see so many animals. He didn't know what to do. But then, he saw how happy they all were to share. He realized that being rich with friends is much better than being rich with things.

From then on, the fox was always kind and shared with others. And all the animals lived happily ever after. The end.

When Lily got home, she showed the rose to her mom. Her mom was very happy to see the unique rose. She put the rose in a vase with water. Lily and her mom sat down and finished their lunch together. They talked about the pretty rose, and the big garden where it grew.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a pet bird named Blue. Blue was a very obedient bird. He always listened to Tim.

One day, Tim and Blue went to a big field. The field was full of wheat. The wheat was tall and golden. Tim and Blue loved to play in the wheat field.

Tim said to Blue, "Let's play a game!" Tim held Blue in his hand and said, "I will release you, and you fly up high. Then, come back to me." Blue nodded. Tim released Blue, and he flew up high into the sky. Blue loved to fly! After a while, Blue came back to Tim, just like he said he would. They played this game all day and had lots of fun.

Just then, a small worm crawled out of the hole. The worm said, "Hi! I'm Wally the Worm. I live in this hole. Do you want to be my friend?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I would like to be your friend, Wally!"

Lily and Wally played together all day. They laughed and had so much fun. When it was time for Lily to go home, she said, "Thank you, Wally, for being my friend and playing with me today." Wally smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily, for being my friend too. I hope we can play together again soon!" And they both waved goodbye as Lily went home, knowing they had made a new friend in each other.

Sally and Fred worked together to unlock the box. Inside the box, they found a big, red hat. Sally put the hat on her head. She looked funny and felt embarrassed. All her friends laughed and said, "Sally, you look so funny with that big, red hat!"

Sally laughed too and shared the hat with her friends. They all took turns wearing the big, red hat and laughing together. In the end, they put the hat back in the box and locked it again. They knew they could always unlock it if they wanted to have more fun.

Tim felt better and decided to draw the spider too. After he finished his drawings, he showed them to his mom. She was proud of him and hung his drawings on the fridge. Tim was happy that he could write and draw about his new insect friends.

Timmy kicked the shiny blue marble towards Billy. Billy was so excited that he didn't notice that Timmy had kicked it too hard. The marble went flying and landed in a nearby pond. Billy was sad that he lost the game, but Timmy knew that he had set up a payoff. He went to the pond and retrieved his favorite marble. Billy learned a lesson about being ignorant and Timmy learned that it's important to be a good friend.

Once upon a time, a little bunny named Benny was hopping around in the meadow. He saw a carrot patch and felt hungry. He wanted to eat a carrot but there was a fence around it. Benny saw a hole in the fence and thought he could squeeze through. He tried, but he seemed too big. 

Just then, Benny heard a friendly voice. It was his friend, a little mouse named Mickey. Mickey said, "Hi Benny, what are you doing?" Benny replied, "I want to eat a carrot, but I can't get through the fence." Mickey said, "Don't worry, I know a way in." 

Mickey showed Benny a secret entrance and they both went in. Benny was so happy to see all the available carrots. He ate until his tummy was full. As they were leaving, Benny said, "Thanks, Mickey. You're a good friend." Mickey replied, "No problem, Benny. That's what friends are for." 

From that day on, Benny and Mickey went on many adventures together. They learned that sometimes things may seem difficult, but with the help of a friend, anything is possible. They also learned to always share and help each other out.

Sara and Tom were playing near the stream. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. Sara found a big stone that was round and smooth. She wanted to show it to Tom.

"Look, Tom, look at my stone!" she said, holding it up.

Tom looked at the stone and frowned. He wanted a big stone too, but he could not find one. He felt angry and jealous.

"That's not your stone, Sara, that's my stone!" he said, grabbing it from her hand.

"No, it's not, it's mine! I found it first!" Sara said, pulling it back.

They started to tug and pull on the stone, each trying to keep it for themselves. They did not see the stream getting closer and closer.

Suddenly, Tom gave a hard slap to Sara's hand. Sara let go of the stone and cried out. The stone fell into the stream and sank to the bottom.

"Ow, Tom, that hurt! Why did you slap me?" Sara said, rubbing her hand.

"I wanted the stone, it was mine!" Tom said, but he felt sorry for making Sara cry.

He looked at the stream and saw the stone was gone. He felt sad and silly.

"I'm sorry, Sara, I was mean. The stone was yours, you found it. But now it's gone, we can't get it back." he said.

Sara stopped crying and looked at Tom. She saw he was sorry and sad too.

"It's okay, Tom, I forgive you. The stone was just an ordinary stone, it was not special. We can find more stones, or play something else. We are still friends, right?" she said.

Tom nodded and smiled. He hugged Sara and said, "Yes, we are still friends. I'm sorry I slapped you. Let's play something else."

They held hands and walked away from the stream, looking for a new game to play. They forgot about the stone and the slap, and had fun together.

Anna and Ben are best friends. They like to play in the park with their dog, Spot. Spot is a loyal dog. He always follows them and protects them from danger.

One day, they hear a loud noise in the bushes. They are scared. They think it is a monster. They run to hide behind a tree. Spot barks at the noise.

"Spot, come here!" Anna calls. "It is not safe!"

But Spot does not listen. He wants to find out what the noise is. He runs to the bushes.

"Spot, no!" Ben shouts. "You are brave, but you are silly!"

Anna and Ben hear a growl and a whimper. They are very worried. They hope Spot is okay.

They peek from behind the tree. They see Spot and a small cat. The cat is hurt. It has a thorn in its paw. Spot is licking the cat's wound. He is trying to help the cat.

Anna and Ben are surprised. They realize the noise was not a monster. It was a cat in pain.

They come out from behind the tree. They walk to Spot and the cat. They pet them gently.

"Good boy, Spot," Anna says. "You are not silly. You are kind."

"Sorry, Spot," Ben says. "You are not brave. You are heroic."

The cat purrs and rubs against Spot. Spot wags his tail. He is happy.

Anna has an idea. She says, "Let's take the cat home. We can take care of it. Maybe it can be our new friend."

Ben agrees. He says, "Yes, let's do that. Spot will like that too. He likes to make new friends."

They pick up the cat and carry it home. Spot follows them. He is a loyal dog. He always stays with them and loves them.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that courage is not only about facing danger, but also about showing compassion and kindness to others. It also shows that loyalty is a valuable trait in a friend. Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The loud noise in the bushes sets up the expectation of a monster, but the payoff is a cat in need of help. Spot's loyalty and bravery are foreshadowed by his behavior in the park, and pay off by his actions in the bushes.

There were many horses at the farm. Some were black, some were brown, some were white. They had long hair and shiny eyes. Anna thought they were adorable. She wanted to pet them and hug them.

She saw a man with a whip. He was making the horses jump over fences and do tricks. He looked mean. Anna did not like him. She wondered why he needed a whip. She thought the horses did not like him either.

She saw a girl with a pink helmet. She was riding a small horse. She looked happy. She did not have a whip. She had a carrot. She gave the carrot to the horse when they finished. The horse licked her hand. Anna liked her. She wanted to be her friend.

She ran to the girl and said: "Hi, I'm Anna. I love your horse. Can I ride him too?"

The girl smiled and said: "Hi, I'm Lily. This is Sparky. He's my horse. He's very gentle and smart. You can ride him if you want. But you have to promise me something."

Anna nodded eagerly and said: "What do I have to promise?"

Lily said: "You have to promise to be nice to him. You have to promise not to use a whip. You have to promise to give him a carrot when you're done. Can you promise that?"

Anna said: "Yes, I can promise that. I would never hurt a horse. I love horses. They are my favorite animals."

Lily said: "OK, then. Come on, I'll help you get on. Sparky, this is Anna. She's going to ride you for a little while. Be good to her, OK?"

Sparky neighed softly and nuzzled Anna's cheek. Anna felt happy. She climbed on his back and held his mane. Lily walked beside them and showed her how to steer and stop. Anna felt like she was flying. She felt like she was dreaming.

She thanked Lily and Sparky for the ride. She gave Sparky a carrot and a hug. She said: "You are the best horse ever. I hope I can see you again."

Lily said: "You're welcome. You are a good rider. I hope you can come back too. Maybe next time we can ride together."

Anna said: "That would be awesome. Can we be friends?"

Lily said: "Of course we can be friends. Friends who love horses."

They smiled and hugged. They made a new promise. A promise to be friends forever.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make different things with their blocks, cars, and dolls. Lily had an idea. She wanted to make a surprise for Mommy and Daddy. She whispered to Ben, "Let's attach this alarm to the door. When they open it, it will make a loud noise and they will be so surprised!"

Ben nodded and smiled. He thought it was a fun idea. He helped Lily find some tape and a string. They attached the alarm to the door with the tape and tied the string to the handle. They hid behind the couch and waited for Mommy and Daddy to come home.

Soon, they heard the key in the lock. They giggled and held their breath. Mommy and Daddy opened the door and the alarm went off. It was very loud and scary. Mommy and Daddy jumped and screamed. They looked around and saw the alarm and the string. They saw Lily and Ben behind the couch. They were not happy.

They walked over to the couch and asked, "Who did this? Who attached the alarm to the door?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They knew they had done something wrong. They felt sorry. They decided to be honest. They said, "We did it. We wanted to make a surprise for you. We are sorry. We didn't mean to scare you."

Mommy and Daddy sighed. They were not angry anymore. They were glad that Lily and Ben were honest. They hugged them and said, "We love you, but please don't do that again. It was not a nice surprise. It was a bad joke. It could have hurt someone or broken something. Next time, think of a better way to surprise us."

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "We are sorry. We love you too. We will think of a better way to surprise you next time."

They helped Mommy and Daddy take off the alarm and the tape and the string. They put away their toys and said sorry again. Mommy and Daddy smiled and said, "It's okay. We forgive you. You are good kids. You are honest kids. Now, let's have some dinner and talk about your day."

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs and worms. Sometimes they found shiny stones or pretty flowers.

"Look, Lily, I found a big root!" Ben said, holding up a long, brown thing. "It was under the ground. I think it belongs to a tree."

"Wow, Ben, that's cool!" Lily said. "Can I see it?"

Ben gave the root to Lily. She felt it with her fingers. It was hard and rough. She saw some tiny holes on it.

"Maybe the bugs live in the holes," she said. "Do you think they are happy there?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe they are. Maybe the root provides them with food and water and a place to hide."

They heard a loud bark. They looked up and saw a big, gray dog running towards them. It had a wet nose and a wagging tail.

"Uh-oh, it's Max!" Ben said. "He likes to chase us and play with us. But he might want our root too. He likes to chew on things."

"Quick, hide the root!" Lily said. "We don't want him to take it away from us or the bugs."

They buried the root under some leaves and ran to the other side of the garden. Max followed them, barking happily. He wanted to play with them, not with the root. He didn't know it was there.

The end.

"Let's open it!" Ben says.

"OK!" Lily says.

He does not see the police. They are behind him. They have guns. They say "Stop! You are under arrest!"

Lily and her brother Max were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run around. Lily saw a big dog with a ball in its mouth. She loved dogs and wanted to pet it.

"Look, Max, a doggy! Can we go and say hello?" she asked her brother.

Max was afraid of dogs. He shook his head and said, "No, Lily, it might bite us. Let's stay away from it."

But Lily did not listen. She ran towards the dog and said, "Hi, doggy, you are so cute! Can I play with your ball?"

The dog did not like strangers. It growled and barked at Lily. It showed its teeth and snapped at her hand. Lily screamed and ran back to Max. She was scared and hurt.

The dog's owner came and apologized. He said, "I'm sorry, little girl, my dog is not very friendly. He doesn't like to share his ball. Are you okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "I'm okay, thank you. But your dog is mean. He scared me and made me cry."

Max hugged his sister and said, "It's okay, Lily, don't cry. You were brave to try to make a new friend. But next time, you should ask before you touch a dog. Some dogs don't like that."

Lily sniffed and said, "Okay, Max, I will. Thank you for being my big brother. You are so kind and smart."

Max smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are my adorable sister. I love you."

They hugged and kissed. Then they went back to playing in the park. They had fun and forgot about the dog. They were happy.

"Here you go, sweetie. Be careful and don't get wet," her mom said, handing her a pink umbrella with flowers.

"Thank you, mom. I love you," Lily said, opening the umbrella and running to the door.

She stepped outside and saw a big puddle. She smiled and jumped into it, making a splash. She laughed and felt the raindrops on her face. She liked the sound of the rain and the smell of the wet grass.

She saw a little bird on a branch, shivering and wet. She felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help. She walked over to the tree and said, "Hello, bird. Are you cold? Do you want to share my umbrella?"

The bird looked at her and nodded. It flew down and landed on her shoulder. Lily held the umbrella over both of them and said, "There, now we are both warm and dry. Do you want to be my friend?"

The bird chirped and nuzzled her cheek. Lily smiled and hugged the bird. She was happy to have a new friend. She said, "What is your name, bird?"

The bird said, "My name is Blue. What is yours?"

"My name is Lily. Nice to meet you, Blue," Lily said.

They talked and played under the umbrella, until Lily's mom called her for lunch. Lily said, "Blue, I have to go now. But you can come with me if you want. Do you want to come?"

Blue said, "Yes, I do. Thank you, Lily. You are very kind."

Lily said, "You're welcome, Blue. You are very sweet."

She removed the umbrella from her shoulder and held it in her hand. She and Blue walked back to the house, where her mom was waiting for them. Lily said, "Mom, this is Blue. He is my new friend. Can he stay for lunch?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course he can, honey. He is very cute. Come on in, both of you. I have some sandwiches and juice for you."

Lily and Blue went inside and enjoyed their lunch. They were very happy and grateful. They had found each other on a rainy day.

Timmy had to stay in the hospital for a long time and he couldn't ride his bike for a while. He learned that it's important to be careful when you ride your bike and to always wear a helmet. Timmy's mom bought him a new helmet and he promised to always wear it when he rode his bike. From that day on, Timmy was always careful and never had another accident.

But her mother did find her. She saw the wet tub and the wet toys and the wet girl. She was not happy. She scolded Sara for being naughty and disobedient. She said Sara could have hurt herself or caught a cold. She said Sara had to go inside and change her clothes and take a nap.

Sara was sorry for what she did. She said sorry to her mother and hugged her. She said she loved her mother and would listen to her next time. Her mother said she loved her too and forgave her. She said she was glad Sara was safe and healthy. She said she wanted Sara to be happy, but also to be careful and respectful.

Sara learned her lesson. She realized that her mother knew what was best for her and that she should trust her. She also learned that playing with water was fun, but only when it was warm and with permission. She decided to be a good girl and obey her mother. She also decided to be more grateful for her mother and her toys. She thought they were very cute and precious.

Sam was a soldier who liked to play with his toy cars and trucks. He had many cars and trucks, but his favorite was a big red fire truck. He always took it with him when he went to the park or to his friend's house.

One day, he went to the park with his mom and his fire truck. He saw a girl named Lily who was playing with a doll. Sam wanted to play with Lily, but he did not like dolls. He thought they were boring and silly. He wanted Lily to play with his fire truck instead.

He went to Lily and said, "Hi, I am Sam. Do you want to play with my fire truck? It is very fun and fast. You can rub the siren and it makes a loud noise."

Lily looked at Sam and said, "No, thank you. I like my doll. She is very pretty and soft. You can rub her hair and it feels nice."

Sam did not listen to Lily. He grabbed her doll and threw it on the ground. He said, "Dolls are not fun. Fire trucks are better. You have to play with my fire truck."

Lily was very sad and angry. She cried and said, "That is not nice. You are a bad soldier. You have to give me back my doll. She is my friend."

Sam did not care. He laughed and said, "No, I will not. You have to play with my fire truck or I will not be your friend."

Lily ran to her mom and told her what Sam did. Her mom was very upset and said, "That is not how you treat other people. You have to be kind and respectful. You have to share and take turns. You have to say sorry to Lily and give her back her doll."

Sam felt uncomfortable. He knew he did something wrong. He did not want to be a bad soldier. He wanted to be a good friend. He went to Lily and said, "I am sorry, Lily. I was mean to you. I should not have taken your doll. Here, you can have it back. Can we still be friends?"

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Sam. I forgive you. You are a good soldier. We can still be friends. Do you want to play with my doll and your fire truck together?"

Sam nodded and said, "Yes, I do. That sounds like fun. Maybe we can rub the siren and the hair and make a new noise."

They hugged and played happily. They learned that they can like different things and still be friends. They learned that they have to be nice and share. They learned that saying sorry and forgiving are important. They learned that being a good soldier means being a good person.

Sam was stubborn and did not stop. He ignored Tom and ran away. He hid behind a tree and waited for Tom to come closer. Then he jumped out and pointed the toy gun at Tom. "Bang, bang, you're dead, cop!" he said.

Tom was not happy. He did not like to lose. He did not fall down and pretend to be dead. He said "No, you missed, I'm still alive. Give me the gun, it's my turn to be the robber."

Sam did not want to give the gun. He liked to be the robber. He said "No, it's still my turn. You have to be the cop. Go away, or I'll shoot you again."

Tom and Sam started to fight over the gun. They pulled and pushed and yelled at each other. They did not see the big dog that came running towards them. The dog was curious and wanted to play. He saw the toy gun and thought it was a stick. He jumped and grabbed the gun with his mouth. He ran away with the gun, wagging his tail.

Tom and Sam stopped fighting. They looked at the dog and the gun. They felt sad and angry. They had lost their toy. They ran after the dog, but the dog was faster. He disappeared behind a fence. Tom and Sam could not get the gun back.

They went back to the park. They sat on a bench and did not talk. They wished they had not been stubborn and ignored each other. They wished they had shared the gun and played nicely. They learned a lesson. They said they were sorry and hugged. They decided to be friends again and play something else. They hoped the dog would not break the gun and bring it back someday.

Tom is a little boy who likes to play with his toy cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He keeps them in a big box under his bed. Every morning, he wakes up and runs to his box to choose a car to play with.

One day, he wakes up and sees that his box is not under his bed. He looks around and sees that his sister, Anna, has taken his box to her room. He is very angry and wants his box back. He runs to her door and tries to open it, but it is locked. He pulls the handle hard, but it does not move.

"Anna, give me my box!" he shouts. "Those are my cars, not yours!"

"Go away, Tom!" Anna says from inside. "I want to play with your cars. They are fun and pretty. You can't have them!"

Tom is very sad and mad. He does not know what to do. He sits on the floor and cries. He hears his mom coming upstairs. She sees him and asks him what is wrong.

"Anna took my box of cars and locked her door!" he tells her. "She won't give them back!"

Mom hugs him and says, "I'm sorry, Tom. That was not nice of Anna. But you have to be calm and not yell. Maybe she will share with you if you ask her nicely. Let me talk to her, okay?"

Mom knocks on Anna's door and says, "Anna, can you please open the door? I want to talk to you and Tom."

Anna hears her mom and feels a little sorry. She knows she was not fair to Tom. She unlocks the door and opens it. She sees Tom and his mom waiting outside.

"Hi, Anna," mom says. "Why did you take Tom's box of cars without asking him?"

Anna looks down and says, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play with them. They are so cool and shiny. I don't have any cars like that."

Mom says, "I understand, Anna. But you have to respect Tom's things. They are his, and he loves them. How would you feel if he took your dolls or your books without asking you?"

Anna thinks and says, "I would feel sad and mad, too. I wouldn't like that."

Mom says, "That's right, Anna. So, what do you think you should do now?"

Anna looks at Tom and says, "I'm sorry, Tom. I shouldn't have taken your box of cars. Can I give it back to you and maybe play with you sometimes?"

Tom smiles and says, "Yes, Anna. Thank you for saying sorry. I forgive you. And you can play with me and my cars sometimes, if you ask me first."

Anna and Tom hug and say, "I love you, brother/sister."

Mom smiles and says, "I'm proud of you, Anna and Tom. You are good kids. Now, why don't you go downstairs and have some breakfast? I made pancakes and juice for you."

Anna and Tom say, "Yay! We love pancakes and juice!" They take the box of cars and run downstairs, happy and hungry. Mom follows them, happy and calm.

Sara loved to play in the garden with her mom. She liked to smell the flowers and watch the bees and butterflies. Her mom taught her the names of the flowers, like rose, daisy, and sunflower. Sara's favorite was the rose, because it was red and pretty and smelled sweet.

One day, Sara saw a new rose on a tall stem. It was higher than the other roses, and it looked very bright and shiny. Sara wanted to smell it and touch it, but it was too far for her. She stretched her arm as much as she could, but she still could not reach it.

"Mom, can you help me?" Sara asked. "I want to see the new rose."

Her mom smiled and came over. She lifted Sara up and held her close to the rose. Sara was happy and excited. She smelled the rose and touched its petals gently.

"Be careful, Sara," her mom said. "The rose has thorns. They can hurt you if you are not careful."

Sara nodded and looked at the thorns. They were sharp and pointy. She wondered why the rose had thorns. She asked her mom.

"The rose has thorns to protect itself," her mom explained. "Some animals like to eat roses, or break them, or take them away. The thorns make them go away. The rose wants to stay safe and beautiful."

Sara understood. She thought the rose was smart and brave. She also thought the rose was lonely. It was the only one on the tall stem, and it had no friends.

"Mom, can we take the rose home?" Sara asked. "We can put it in a vase and give it water and love. Then it will not be lonely anymore."

Her mom looked at the rose and thought for a moment. She saw that the rose was the only one available on the tall stem, and that it was very special. She also saw that Sara loved the rose very much, and that she wanted to make it happy.

"Okay, Sara," her mom said. "We can take the rose home. But we have to be very careful and gentle. We don't want to hurt the rose or ourselves."

Sara smiled and hugged her mom. She thanked her and said she was the best mom ever. Her mom smiled and kissed her. She took a pair of scissors and cut the rose carefully. She wrapped it in a paper and gave it to Sara.

Sara held the rose carefully and proudly. She looked at it and whispered, "Don't worry, rose. You are coming home with me. You will have a new friend. I will take good care of you. I love you, rose."

"Here, fox, we have some food and water for you," Mia said softly. "Don't be afraid. We want to help you."

The fox smelled the food and water. It was very hungry and thirsty. It came out of its hiding place and ate the sandwich and drank the water. It felt better. It licked Mia's hand to say thank you.

Mia smiled. She gently pulled out the thorn from the fox's paw. The fox whimpered a little, but then wagged its tail. It was grateful to Mia for being kind.

"Wow, Mia, you are brave and nice," Tom said. "You made the fox happy."

Mia hugged Tom. "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. And so is the fox."

The fox looked at Mia and Tom. It felt safe and loved. It decided to stay with them for a while. They played together in the park until it was time to go home.

But then, Tom saw a real shield in the garage. It was shiny and metal and had a lion on it. He wanted to have it for himself. He ran to the garage and took the shield. He left his cardboard shield behind.

Anna saw what Tom did and was sad. She liked their game and their pretend shields. She followed Tom and asked him to share the shield.

"Please, Tom, can I have a turn with the shield? It is so pretty and I want to be a brave princess too."

"No, Anna, this is my shield now. You can have the old one. It is boring and fake. Go away!"

Anna felt hurt and angry. She did not want to play with Tom anymore. She took the cardboard shield and went to the other side of the garden. She found a nice spot under a tree and made a new game with her crown and some flowers.

Tom tried to play with the metal shield, but he soon got bored. It was heavy and hard and made his arm hurt. He could not pretend to fight dragons with it. He could not pretend to save Anna with it. He missed his sister and their fun game.

He looked at the cardboard shield and felt sorry. He had been mean and selfish. He had spoiled their game and their friendship. He wanted to say sorry to Anna and make up with her.

He took the metal shield back to the garage and ran to the tree where Anna was. He saw her smiling and playing with her crown and flowers. He felt ashamed.

"Anna, I am sorry. I was wrong to take the shield and not share with you. I was silly and greedy. Can you forgive me?"

Anna looked at Tom and saw that he was sincere. She felt happy and relieved. She loved her brother and wanted to play with him again.

"Of course, Tom, I forgive you. You are my brother and my friend. Come and join me. We can play knights and princesses again. We can use both shields. They are both good and fun."

Tom hugged Anna and thanked her. He took the cardboard shield and put it on his arm. He felt light and free. He and Anna played together and had a wonderful time.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Don't be greedy and selfish. Don't spoil your fun and your friendship. Be kind and generous.

Tom smiled. "That's okay. I forgive you. You are my sister and I love you. And you are lucky, because I have some ice cream in the freezer. Do you want some?"

Anna's eyes lit up. "Yes, please! I love ice cream. Ice cream is yummy. Ice cream is good to freeze. Thank you, Tom. You are my brother and I love you. And you are lucky, too, because I have some sprinkles in the cupboard. Do you want some?"

Tom nodded. "Yes, please! I love sprinkles. Sprinkles are colorful and crunchy and fun. Thank you, Anna. You are the best sister ever."

They hugged and then went to the freezer and the cupboard. They got the ice cream and the sprinkles and made themselves a delicious treat. They ate it happily and forgot about the frozen eggs. They were lucky to have each other and to have ice cream and sprinkles. They were happy.

From that day on, the rabbit learned that it's always better to share and be kind to others. He became a better friend and everyone liked him more. The moral of the story is that sharing and kindness are very important things to have in life.

Her mom answered, "It's because there's a big cloud covering the sun."

Lily looked up and saw that her mom was right. She felt sad because she wanted to play outside, but it was too dark. Suddenly, she had an idea. She ran inside and asked her mom for a flashlight. Her mom gave her one and Lily ran back outside. She touched the flowers with the light and they looked even more beautiful in the dark. She was happy again and forgot about the gloomy cloud.

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play with toys, draw pictures and talk to each other. Sometimes they talked about funny things, like what animals would say if they could talk. Sometimes they talked about scary things, like monsters and ghosts. And sometimes they talked about weird things, like what was inside their heads.

One day, they decided to play a game. They pretended they were doctors and they had to fix a broken brain. They found a big ball of clay and shaped it like a brain. They used sticks and stones and leaves to make tools and bandages. They took turns being the doctor and the patient.

"Your brain is very sick," Max said, holding a stick like a needle. "It has a lot of bugs and worms. I have to poke them out."

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily said, lying on the ground. "That hurts! Be careful, doctor!"

"Don't worry, patient," Max said. "I know what I'm doing. I'm a very good doctor. I learned from a book."

"What book?" Lily asked.

"A book about brains," Max said. "It had a lot of big words and pictures. I didn't understand everything, but I learned some things. Like, your brain has different parts that do different things. And your brain is what makes you talk and think and feel."

"Really?" Lily said. "That's amazing. And weird. How does a brain do that?"

"I don't know," Max said. "It's a mystery. Maybe we can find out if we look inside."

He lifted the clay brain and broke it in half. He showed Lily the inside. It was smooth and gray and had no bugs or worms.

"Wow," Lily said. "Is that what a real brain looks like?"

"I think so," Max said. "But it doesn't look like much. How can it do so much?"

They stared at the clay brain, wondering and talking. They didn't notice that their dog, Spot, had sneaked up behind them. He smelled the clay and thought it was a snack. He grabbed it with his mouth and ran away.

"Hey!" Max shouted. "Spot, come back! That's our brain!"

They chased after him, but he was too fast. He ran to the pond and threw the clay brain into the water. It sank to the bottom and broke into pieces.

"Oh, no!" Lily cried. "Our brain is gone!"

They were very sad. They had lost their game and their brain. They sat by the pond and hugged each other.

"Maybe we can make another one," Max said.

"Maybe," Lily said. "But it won't be the same. It won't be our brain."

They looked at the pond and saw their reflections. They saw their eyes and noses and mouths. They saw their faces and expressions. They saw themselves.

They smiled.

"Maybe we don't need a brain," Lily said.

"Why not?" Max asked.

"Because we have each other," Lily said. "And we can still talk and think and feel. And that's what matters."

They hugged again. They were still best friends. And they were happy.

Sam looks at Tim's folder. He sees the dog. He wants the dog. He thinks, "Maybe I can take Tim's folder and give him mine. Then I can have the interesting folder and he can have the boring folder." He waits for the teacher to look away. Then he swaps the folders. He smiles. Tim does not see the swap. He is busy with his work.

The teacher comes back. She says, "Time is up. Give me your folders. I will check your work." She takes the folders. She looks at Tim's folder. She sees the cat. She says, "Tim, this is not your folder. This is Sam's folder. Why do you have Sam's folder?" Tim is confused. He says, "I do not know. I had a dog folder. Where is my dog folder?" The teacher looks at Sam's folder. She sees the dog. She says, "Sam, this is not your folder. This is Tim's folder. Why do you have Tim's folder?" Sam is scared. He says, "I do not know. I had a cat folder. I do not like cats."

The teacher is angry. She says, "Sam, you are lying. You swapped the folders. You wanted Tim's folder and you gave him yours. That is not nice. That is cheating. You have to say sorry to Tim and give him back his folder. And you have to do your work again. And you have to learn to like cats. They are not boring. They are also interesting." Sam is ashamed. He says, "Sorry, Tim. Sorry, teacher. I was wrong. I will not do that again." He gives Tim back his folder. He takes his own folder. He seats and does his work. He looks at the cat. He thinks, "Maybe the cat is not so bad. Maybe I can learn something from the cat."

The moral of the story is: Do not cheat. Do your own work. Be happy with what you have. Respect your friends. Be open to new things.

One day, Anna and Ben see a big sign. The sign says "Pool Closed". Anna and Ben are sad. They want to swim in the pool. They ask their mom why the pool is closed.

Mom says "The pool is closed because it is dirty. Some people did not follow the rules. They threw trash and food in the water. That is bad. The pool needs to be cleaned."

Anna and Ben nod. They understand. They do not like dirty water. They always follow the rules. They do not throw trash and food in the water. They say "Sorry, pool. We hope you get clean soon."

Mom says "Don't worry, Anna and Ben. The pool will open again in a few days. Then you can swim and have fun again. But for now, we have to stay away from the pool. We can do other things. We can read books, play games, or go to the park."

Anna and Ben smile. They love books, games, and the park. They hug their mom. They say "Okay, mom. We will stay away from the pool. We will do other things. We will wait for the pool to open again. We love you, mom. And we love the pool."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the snow. They make a snowman with a hat and a carrot nose. They give him two sticks for arms.

But the snowman is cold. He has no mittens. Lily and Ben look for mittens. They find one red mitten and one blue mitten. They are big mittens. They are too big for Lily and Ben.

"Let's give the mittens to the snowman," Lily says. "He will be warm and happy."

"Good idea," Ben says. They put the mittens on the snowman's stick arms. The snowman smiles.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben," the snowman says. "You are very kind. I like my mittens. They are big and cozy."

Lily and Ben are happy. They hug the snowman. They play with him until it is time to go home. They say goodbye to the snowman. They hope he will stay warm and happy.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide on the grass. They saw an enormous dog near the fence. The dog was black and furry and had big teeth.

"Wow, look at that dog!" Ben said. "He is so big and strong. I want to pet him."

"No, Ben, don't go there!" Anna said. "He might be angry or bite you. He is not our dog. We don't know him."

But Ben did not listen to Anna. He ran to the fence and called the dog. "Hey, dog, come here! You are so cool. I want to be your friend."

The dog heard Ben and came to the fence. He looked at Ben with his yellow eyes. He did not like Ben. He did not want to be his friend. He growled and barked and showed his teeth.

"Go away, dog!" Ben said. He was scared. He tried to run back to Anna. But it was too late. The dog jumped over the fence and chased Ben. He caught him and bit him hard. Ben screamed and cried. He was hurt.

Anna ran to Ben and tried to help him. She shouted for help. She was sad and scared. The dog was bad. He did not order Ben. He hurt him. Anna and Ben did not like the dog. They did not like the park. They wanted to go home.

Lily liked to draw with her pen. She drew flowers and stars and cats on her paper. She was happy when she drew.

But her brother Tom did not like her pen. He wanted to play with it. He said, "Give me your pen, Lily. It is mine now."

Lily said, "No, Tom. It is my pen. I got it from Mom. You have your own toys. Go away."

Tom was angry. He grabbed the pen from Lily's hand. He ran to the door. He said, "Ha ha, I have your pen. You can't have it back."

Lily was sad. She cried. She wanted her pen. She followed Tom to the door. She said, "Tom, please give me my pen. It is not nice to take things."

But Tom was mean. He opened the door and threw the pen outside. He said, "There, your pen is gone. You can't draw anymore." He slammed the door and locked it. He laughed.

Lily was very sad. She banged on the door. She said, "Tom, open the door. You are bad. You are harsh. You hurt me."

But Tom did not open the door. He ignored Lily. He played with his toys.

Lily cried and cried. She wished she had her pen. She wished Tom was nice. She wished Mom was home.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they found a big box in the garage. They had a creative idea. They wanted to become pirates and sail the seas.

They cut holes in the box for windows and a door. They drew a flag and a map on the box. They put on hats and scarves and pretended to have swords. They said, "Ahoy, matey! We are the best pirates ever!"

They took the box outside and put it on the grass. They climbed inside and started to play. They looked for treasure and fought with other pirates. They had a lot of fun.

But then, it started to rain. The rain was very heavy and loud. The box got wet and soggy. The holes got bigger and the drawings got blurry. The box started to fall apart. Lily and Tom got scared and sad.

They ran back to the garage and left the box behind. They cried and hugged each other. They said, "We are not pirates anymore. We are just wet and cold. Our box is ruined. Our game is over."

They wished they had a better box. They wished they had a better week. They wished they had a better ending.

Tom liked to play with his toy cars. He had many cars of different colors and sizes. He liked to make them zoom on the floor and pretend they were racing. His favorite car was a gray one with a big number four on the side. He called it his fast car.

One day, Tom's mom said they had to go to the store. She told Tom to bring one toy to play with in the car. Tom picked his fast car and put it in his pocket. He was happy to zoom it on the seat and the window. He made vroom-vroom noises and smiled.

At the store, Tom's mom said he had to stay close to her and hold her hand. She said there were many people and things in the store and he could get lost or hurt. Tom nodded and held his mom's hand. But he still had his fast car in his pocket. He wanted to zoom it on the shelves and the carts. He thought it would be fun.

When his mom was looking at some clothes, Tom saw a big ramp near the door. It was for people who had wheels to go up and down. Tom thought it would be a great place to zoom his fast car. He let go of his mom's hand and ran to the ramp. He took out his fast car and threw it on the ramp. He watched it zoom down and up and down again. He clapped and laughed.

But then he saw his mom. She was looking for him and she looked scared and angry. She saw him and the fast car on the ramp. She ran to him and grabbed him. She said he was very naughty and he could have lost his fast car or himself. She said he had to say sorry and never do that again. Tom felt bad. He said sorry and hugged his mom. He said he loved her and his fast car. He said he would be good and stay with her. His mom said she loved him too and she was glad he was safe. She said he could keep his fast car but he had to be careful with it. Tom nodded and held his mom's hand. He put his fast car back in his pocket. He still liked to zoom it, but only when it was safe.

Lila was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She lived near a big airport, where she could see many jets fly in the sky. She liked to watch them and wonder where they were going.

One day, she saw a new jet. It was shiny and red, with a big star on its side. It looked very fast and cool. Lila wanted to see it up close. She felt an urge to go to the airport and find it.

She put on her shoes and coat and ran out of the house. She did not tell her mom, because she knew she would say no. She crossed the street and followed the fence that surrounded the airport. She looked for a hole or a gate where she could get in.

She found one, and squeezed through. She ran across the grass and the concrete, looking for the red jet. She saw many other jets, but not the one she wanted. She felt scared and lost. She wished she had stayed home.

"Hey, you! What are you doing here?" a loud voice shouted. Lila turned and saw a man in a blue uniform. He looked angry and had a walkie-talkie in his hand. He was coming towards her.

Lila was very afraid. She did not know what to say. She started to cry.

"Please don't hurt me," she sobbed. "I just wanted to see the red jet. It's so pretty."

The man stopped and looked at her. He saw that she was just a little girl, and felt sorry for her.

"Where is your mom?" he asked gently. "You shouldn't be here. It's dangerous."

Lila sniffed and wiped her eyes. She told him where she lived and how she got here.

The man shook his head. He picked up his walkie-talkie and called for help. He told Lila that he would take her back to her mom, and that she should never do this again.

Lila nodded. She felt sorry too. She realized that she had been very naughty and foolish. She missed her mom and wanted to hug her.

She also saw the red jet, parked on the other side of the airport. It was still shiny and cool, but not as much as before.

She decided that she liked watching jets from afar better than chasing them. She hoped that the man and her mom would not be too mad at her. She learned her lesson.

Mia and Ben were twins who liked to play with the ornaments on the tree. They would take them off and put them back on, or pretend they were toys. One day, they saw a shiny star ornament that was very high on the tree. They wanted to reach it, but they were too small.

"Let's get a chair and stand on it," Mia said.

"OK," Ben said. They dragged a chair from the kitchen and put it near the tree. Mia climbed on the chair and Ben helped her balance. She stretched her arm and tried to grab the star, but it was still too distant.

"Can you get it?" Ben asked.

"No, it's too far," Mia said. She leaned forward a little more, but then the chair wobbled and she fell off. She landed on the floor with a thud and the chair tipped over. The star ornament also fell and broke into pieces.

"Ow!" Mia cried. "That hurt!"

"Oh no!" Ben said. "The star is broken!"

They heard their mom coming from the other room. She had heard the noise and was worried. She saw Mia and Ben on the floor, the chair upside down, and the broken star.

"What happened here?" she asked, looking angry.

Mia and Ben looked at each other and felt scared. They knew they had done something bad. They wanted to say sorry, but they didn't know how. They started to cry.

Mom sighed and knelt down next to them. She hugged them and said, "It's OK, don't cry. I'm not mad at you. I know you were just curious. But you have to be careful, OK? You could have hurt yourself or the tree. And the star was very special. It was a gift from grandma. She made it herself."

Mia and Ben sniffed and nodded. They felt sorry for breaking the star. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, grandma."

Mom smiled and said, "It's OK. I forgive you. And I'm sure grandma will too. She loves you very much. Maybe we can fix the star together, or make a new one. Would you like that?"

Mia and Ben nodded again. They felt better. They said, "Yes, mom. We love you. We love grandma."

Mom kissed them and said, "I love you too. Now, let's clean up this mess and put the ornaments back on the tree. And no more climbing on chairs, OK?"

Mia and Ben said, "OK, mom." They helped mom pick up the pieces of the star and the chair. They put the ornaments back on the tree. They found a new place for the star, where they could see it but not touch it. They looked at it and remembered grandma. They smiled and said, "Thank you, grandma."

Mom smiled too and said, "You're welcome, grandma." She hugged them and said, "You're such good kids. You make me laugh." She tickled them and they laughed. They were happy.

Lily and Ben went to the museum with Mom and Dad. They saw many things that made them say wow. They saw big bones of animals that lived long ago. They saw shiny rocks and stars that glowed. They saw paintings and statues and toys from different places.

Lily liked to point at everything she saw. She pointed at a big fish with sharp teeth. She pointed at a colorful bird with long feathers. She pointed at a doll with a pretty dress. Ben liked to point too, but he also liked to ask questions. He asked Mom and Dad what the things were and how they worked. He asked why the fish had teeth and the bird had feathers. He asked who made the doll and the dress.

Mom and Dad were happy to answer Ben's questions. They told him stories and facts about the things in the museum. They told him the fish was a shark and the bird was a peacock. They told him the doll and the dress were from China and they were very old. Lily and Ben learned a lot and had fun.

After they saw everything in the museum, they went to the cafeteria. They were hungry and thirsty. They looked at the menu and saw many yummy things. They saw sandwiches and salads and soups. They saw cookies and cakes and ice cream. They saw juice and milk and water.

Lily and Ben each chose what they wanted to eat and drink. Lily chose a cheese sandwich and a glass of juice. Ben chose a chicken soup and a glass of milk. They also shared a big cookie with chocolate chips. Mom and Dad chose what they wanted too. They all sat at a table and enjoyed their yummy food. They talked about what they liked best in the museum and what they wanted to see next time. They were happy and full.

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to play together. They had a big box of toys that they shared. Sometimes they fought over the toys, but most of the time they were nice to each other.

One day, it was very hot outside. Tom and Jen felt sweaty and thirsty. They wanted something cold to drink. They saw a lemonade stand on the street. They ran to the stand and asked for two cups of lemonade.

"Sorry, kids, I only have one cup left," said the lady who ran the stand. "You can split it if you want."

Tom and Jen looked at each other. They both wanted the whole cup of lemonade. They both felt very hot and dry. They both reached for the cup at the same time.

"Let go, it's mine!" said Tom.

"No, it's mine!" said Jen.

They pulled and tugged on the cup. They did not notice that the lemonade was spilling out of the cup. They did not notice that the lady was watching them with a sad face.

Suddenly, the cup broke in half. The lemonade was gone. Tom and Jen were left with two pieces of plastic. They looked at each other. They felt very silly and sorry.

"I'm sorry, Tom," said Jen.

"I'm sorry, Jen," said Tom.

They hugged each other and said they were sorry to the lady too.

The lady smiled and said, "It's okay, kids. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. That's what matters. You know what? I have a surprise for you. I have another jug of lemonade in the back. I'll give you each a cup for free. You are very generous to share with each other."

Tom and Jen thanked the lady and took their cups of lemonade. They drank the cold and sweet drink and felt much better. They learned that sharing is better than fighting. They learned that being generous is better than being greedy. They learned that lemonade is better than heat.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One morning, they both want to use the shower first. They run to the bathroom and push each other.

"I want to shower first!" Lily says.

Tom was a fisherman who liked to catch fish in the lake. He had a small boat and a big net. He was popular with the people in the town, because he always shared his fish with them.

One day, a little girl named Lily came to the lake. She saw Tom in his boat and waved to him. She wanted to see the fish he caught. She asked her mom if she could go to the boat. Her mom said yes, but she had to be careful.

Lily ran to the shore and called to Tom. "Hello, fisherman! Can I see your fish, please?" she requested.

Tom smiled and rowed his boat to the shore. He lifted his net and showed Lily his fish. There were many fish of different colors and sizes. Lily was amazed and happy. She pointed to a yellow fish and said, "That one is pretty. Can I have it, please?"

Tom nodded and gave Lily the yellow fish. He said, "You can have it, but you have to take good care of it. It is a live fish, not a toy. You have to put it in water and feed it every day."

Lily was a little girl who liked to play in the garden. She had a big sunflower that she watered every day. She wanted it to grow tall and strong.

One day, she saw a bee buzzing around the sunflower. She was curious and asked, "Hello, bee. What are you doing?"

The bee answered, "Hello, Lily. I am looking for nectar. Nectar is sweet and good for me. Your sunflower has a lot of nectar."

Lily smiled and said, "That is nice. Can I have some nectar too?"

The bee said, "No, Lily. Nectar is for bees. You can have honey. Honey is made from nectar. Honey is also sweet and good for you."

Lily said, "Thank you, bee. Where can I find honey?"

The bee said, "You can find honey in my hive. My hive is in the big tree over there. But be careful, Lily. There are many bees in my hive. They will sting you if you get too close. They are protecting the queen. The queen is the most important bee. She makes more bees."

Lily said, "Wow, the queen sounds very special. Can I see her?"

The bee said, "No, Lily. The queen is very busy. She does not like visitors. She stays in the center of the hive. It is very hot there. She needs the heat to keep her eggs warm."

Lily said, "I see. Well, thank you for telling me, bee. You are very smart and kind. I will not bother the queen. I will go and look for some honey. Goodbye, bee."

The bee said, "Goodbye, Lily. Have a nice day. And remember, do not touch the hive. It is not safe for you."

"I'm sorry, Sam. I used the wrong bottle. That was not glue. That was hot sauce. It is spicy. It hurts," Tom said.

Sam was angry. He did not forgive Tom. He threw his car at Tom. It hit Tom's head. Tom cried.

Both brothers were hurt. They went inside. Their mom saw them. She was mad. She scolded them. She took away their toy cars. She gave them ice and water.

Sam and Tom learned a lesson. They should not use things they do not know. They should ask for help. They should be careful. They should be kind.

Anna loved to ride her bike. She rode it every day in the park with her mom and dad. She liked to go fast and feel the wind in her hair. She also liked to see the animals in the park, like the birds, the squirrels and the dogs.

One day, she saw a big dog that was barking loudly. It had a collar and a leash, but no one was holding it. Anna was curious and wanted to pet the dog. She rode her bike closer to the dog and said, "Hello, doggy. You are cute. Can I touch you?"

The dog did not like Anna. It growled and showed its teeth. It jumped on Anna and bit her arm. Anna screamed and fell off her bike. She was hurt and frightened. The dog ran away.

Mom and dad heard Anna scream and ran to her. They saw the blood on her arm and the bite marks. They were scared and angry. They picked up Anna and her bike and took her to the car. They drove to the veterinarian.

The veterinarian was a nice lady who helped animals. She looked at Anna's arm and said, "Oh, dear. This is a bad bite. You need a shot and some stitches. It will hurt, but it will make you better."

Anna did not want a shot or stitches. She cried and said, "No, no, no. I don't want it. Please, don't hurt me."

The veterinarian said, "I'm sorry, Anna. But you have to do it. The dog might have a disease that can make you sick. The shot and the stitches will protect you. I will be gentle and fast. You can hold your mom's hand and close your eyes."

Anna did not listen. She kicked and screamed and tried to get away. She was too frightened to let the veterinarian help her. She made a big fuss and a big mess. The veterinarian could not do her job. She said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I can't treat Anna like this. She needs to calm down and cooperate. Otherwise, she might get an infection or worse. You have to take her to the hospital."

Mom and dad were sad and worried. They took Anna to the hospital. Anna did not like the hospital. It was big and noisy and scary. There were many people and machines and needles. Anna had to wait a long time and see many doctors. She had to get a shot and stitches and a bandage. She had to stay in a bed and take medicine. She missed her bike and her park and her animals. She wished she never saw the big dog. She wished she never rode her bike that day. She wished she listened to the veterinarian. She learned a hard lesson. She was not happy. The end.

Tom and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the park and share their toys. One day, they saw a big pond with many fish and shrimp. They wanted to catch some and take them home.

"Let's make a promise," Tom said. "We will only catch one shrimp each and let the others go. We will not hurt them or keep them too long."

"OK, I promise," Sam said. They found a net and a bucket and went to the pond.

They were very alert and watched the water. They saw many shrimp swimming and jumping. They tried to catch them with the net, but they were too fast and smart. They only caught one shrimp each after a long time.

"Look, I got a big one!" Tom said, holding his shrimp.

"Me too!" Sam said, showing his shrimp. They put them in the bucket and looked at them. They were very pretty and colorful.

But then, they heard a loud splash. They turned around and saw a big fish jumping out of the pond. It had a big mouth and sharp teeth. It looked hungry and angry.

"Run!" Tom shouted. He grabbed the bucket and ran away with Sam. The fish chased them and tried to bite them. They were very scared and ran as fast as they could.

They reached the park gate and threw the bucket over the fence. The fish could not follow them and went back to the pond. Tom and Sam were safe, but they lost their shrimp.

They were very sad and sorry. They realized they had broken their promise and hurt the shrimp and the fish. They learned a lesson: they should not take things that do not belong to them and respect the animals and their home.

They said sorry to the pond and the fish and the shrimp. They hoped they would forgive them. They decided to never catch shrimp again and only watch them from far away. They hugged each other and went home. They were still best friends.

Sara was a lazy girl who did not like to help her mom and dad. She only wanted to watch TV and play with her toys. One day, a big package came to their house. Sara was curious and ran to see what was inside.

"Can I open it, mom?" she asked.

"No, Sara, this package is for your cousin Lily. She is sick and we want to make her happy. You have to wait until we go to visit her," mom said.

Sara was not happy. She wanted to see the package. She thought maybe there was a new toy or a book or a dress for her. She did not care about Lily. She was selfish.

When mom and dad were busy, Sara sneaked to the package and tried to open it. She ripped the paper and saw a big teddy bear. She smiled and grabbed it. She wanted to keep it for herself.

But then she heard a voice. It was the teddy bear. It blinked its eyes and said, "Hello, Sara. I am a magic teddy bear. I can talk and play with you. But I am not for you. I am for Lily. What will you do?"

There was a town with many old houses. In one house, there was a boy named Tom. Tom liked to play with his toys and read his books. But he did not like to sleep. He always wanted to stay up late and see the stars.

One night, Tom's mom said, "It is time to sleep, Tom. You have to wake up early tomorrow. We are going to visit grandma and grandpa. They live far away, so we have to take a long car ride."

Tom said, "No, mom. I don't want to sleep. I want to see the stars. They are so bright and pretty. Please, mom, let me stay up a little more."

Tom's mom said, "No, Tom. You have to sleep. If you don't sleep, you will be tired and grumpy tomorrow. You won't have fun with grandma and grandpa. And you might miss the stars anyway, because it might rain. Now, go to bed and close your eyes."

Tom was sad and angry. He did not want to miss the stars. He did not want to go to bed. He did not want to listen to his mom. He thought of a plan. He said, "Okay, mom. I will go to bed. But can I have a glass of water first?"

Tom's mom said, "Okay, Tom. But hurry up. I will be right here to tuck you in."

Tom went to the kitchen and got a glass of water. But he also got a flashlight. He hid the flashlight under his pillow. He went back to his room and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Good night."

Tom's mom said, "I love you too, Tom. Good night." She tucked him in and turned off the light.

Tom waited for a few minutes. He heard his mom go to her room. He heard her close the door. He heard her snore. He smiled. He took out his flashlight and turned it on. He pointed it at the window. He saw the stars. He was happy.

But he did not know that his mom was not really asleep. She was just pretending. She wanted to see what Tom would do. She heard him turn on his flashlight. She got up and went to his room. She opened the door and said, "Tom, what are you doing? You are supposed to be asleep. You are not allowed to play with your flashlight at night. You are in trouble, young man."

Tom was scared and sorry. He turned off his flashlight and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to see the stars. They are so beautiful. Please, mom, don't be mad at me."

Tom's mom said, "Tom, I understand that you like the stars. But you have to sleep. Sleep is good for you. It helps you grow and learn and dream. And you can see the stars tomorrow, if it doesn't rain. But you have to promise me that you will never play with your flashlight at night again. It is dangerous and rude. Do you promise?"

Tom said, "Yes, mom. I promise. I will never play with my flashlight at night again. I will sleep. I will be a good boy."

Tom's mom said, "Good. I'm glad you understand. I'm not mad at you, Tom. I love you. But you have to follow the rules. Now, give me a hug and a kiss and go to sleep."

Tom gave his mom a hug and a kiss and said, "I love you, mom. Good night."

Lila was a little girl who liked to explore. One day, she saw a big hill near her house. She wanted to see what was on the other side. She put on her boots and her coat and told her mom she was going out.
