As she walked, she stumbled on a rock and fell down. She scraped her knee and it hurt. She cried a little and rubbed it. Then she heard a voice.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" the voice said.

Lila looked up and saw a man with a long beard and a hat. He was holding a broom and looked angry. He lived in the small house.

"I'm Lila," she said. "I was just exploring. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to bother you."

The man frowned and said, "You shouldn't be here. This is my land. Go away."

Lila was scared and sad. She wanted to be friendly, but the man was not nice. She got up and ran back to the hill. She didn't want to see the man again.

She reached her house and hugged her mom. She told her what happened and showed her her knee.

"Ouch, that looks painful," her mom said. "Let me put a band-aid on it. You were very brave, Lila. But next time, be more careful where you go. You never know who you might meet."

Lila nodded and said, "I know, mom. I won't go to the hill again. It was too unusual."

Lily liked to record her voice with her toy phone. She would sing songs, tell jokes, and make funny noises. She would play back her recordings and laugh. She thought she was very clever.

One day, she saw a big herb garden in her neighbor's yard. She wanted to record the names of the herbs, because they sounded nice. She climbed over the fence and walked around the garden. She saw mint, rosemary, basil, and lavender. She held her phone close to each herb and said its name.

But she did not see the neighbor, Mr. Lee, who was working in his shed. He heard Lily's voice and came out to see what was going on. He was not happy to see Lily in his garden. He said, "Hey, what are you doing here? This is my garden, not yours. You are not allowed to touch my herbs. Go away!"

Lily was scared and ran back to the fence. She dropped her phone on the ground. She climbed over the fence and ran to her house. She was sad and sorry. She did not mean to upset Mr. Lee. She just wanted to record the herbs.

The next day, she decided to go back and say sorry to Mr. Lee. She knocked on his door and waited. He opened the door and saw Lily. He said, "What do you want?"

Lily said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Lee. I was wrong to go into your garden and touch your herbs. I was curious and wanted to record their names. I like how they smell and sound. But I should have asked you first. Please forgive me."

Mr. Lee looked at Lily and saw that she was sincere. He said, "I forgive you, Lily. You are a brave and honest girl. I'm sorry I was angry with you. I like my herbs very much and I don't like anyone to harm them. But I can share them with you, if you want. Do you want to come in and see my shed? I have some tools and books and other things you might find interesting."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, please, Mr. Lee. Thank you for being so friendly and kind. Can I bring my phone and record some of your things?"

Mr. Lee said, "Sure, why not? But only if you promise to be careful and respectful. And maybe you can teach me some of the songs and jokes you record. I like to laugh, too."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, Mr. Lee. And I can teach you some songs and jokes. They are very funny."

They went inside and became friends. Lily learned a lot from Mr. Lee and he learned a lot from Lily. They both enjoyed recording and listening to each other's voices. They both had fun.

The moral of the story is: Be respectful of other people's property and feelings. Be honest and apologize when you make a mistake. Be friendly and open to learn from others. You might find a new friend and have a good time.

One day, Tom and Sam decided to play a game with their coins. They took turns picking a coin from the jar and guessing what it was worth. If they guessed right, they kept the coin. If they guessed wrong, they gave it to the other brother. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot about coins.

But then, Tom found a very special coin. It was bigger than any other coin, and it was shiny and gold. Tom was very excited and showed it to Sam.

"Wow, what a cool coin!" Sam said. "How much do you think it is worth?"

Tom thought hard. He remembered that gold was the most valuable thing in the world. He remembered that his dad had a gold ring that he never took off. He remembered that his mom had a gold necklace that she only wore on special days. He decided that the coin must be worth a lot.

"I think it is worth a hundred dollars!" Tom said proudly.

Sam was amazed. He had never seen a hundred dollars before. He wondered what he could buy with a hundred dollars. He wanted the coin very much. He had an idea.

"Tom, that coin is too big for you. You can't put it in your pocket or your piggy bank. It will get lost or stolen. Why don't you trade it with me? I have a lot of smaller coins that are easier to keep. I will give you ten copper coins for your gold coin. That's a fair deal, right?"

Tom looked at Sam's coins. They were dull and brown. They looked boring and old. He didn't want them. He wanted his gold coin. He shook his head.

"No, Sam. I like my gold coin. It is shiny and pretty. It is worth a lot. I don't want your copper coins. They are not worth much. They are fake."

Sam was angry. He thought Tom was being greedy and silly. He wanted to trick him and take his gold coin. He grabbed the coin from Tom's hand and ran away.

"Hey, give it back!" Tom shouted. He chased after Sam.

They ran around the house, fighting and yelling. They knocked over the jar of coins and spilled them everywhere. They bumped into the table and knocked over a lamp. They made a big mess and a lot of noise.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was going on. She saw the coins, the lamp, and the boys. She was not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you fighting? What is that coin?"

She picked up the gold coin and looked at it. She saw that it had a picture of a pirate and a skull on it. She saw that it had the words "FAKE GOLD" on the edge. She realized that it was not a real coin, but a toy.

She showed it to the boys and explained that it was not worth anything. It was just a fake coin that someone had made for fun. It was not gold, but plastic. It was not shiny, but painted. It was not valuable, but worthless.

The boys were shocked and ashamed. They had fought over a fake coin. They had made a big mess and a lot of noise. They had been foolish and rude.

They said sorry to each other and to their mom. They helped her clean up the coins and the lamp. They put the fake coin back in the jar. They decided to play a different game with their coins. They decided to settle their differences and share their coins. They learned a lesson about coins and about brothers.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look at the waves. Sometimes they saw fish and crabs and shells. They wanted to see a whale, but they never did.

One day, they heard a loud splash. They looked at the water and saw a big, gray thing. It had a long tail and a hole on its head. It made a funny noise, like a whistle. Lily and Ben were very excited. They ran to their mom and dad and pointed at the thing.

"Look, look, a whale!" they shouted.

Mom and dad smiled and came to see. They told Lily and Ben that the thing was indeed a whale, and that it was very rare to see one so close to the shore. They said that whales were very smart and friendly animals, and that they liked to talk to each other.

"Can we talk to the whale?" Lily asked.

"Maybe, if we are very quiet and polite," dad said.

He took out a whistle from his pocket and blew it softly. The whale heard it and came closer. It blew some water from its hole and made another noise, like a question.

"Hello, whale," dad said. "We are happy to see you. What is your name?"

The whale made another noise, like an answer. It sounded like "Ooo-eee".

"Ooo-eee? That's a nice name," dad said. "I'm dad, and this is mom, and these are Lily and Ben. We are humans."

The whale nodded and made a noise, like a greeting.

"Hello, Ooo-eee," Lily and Ben said.

They smiled and waved at the whale. The whale smiled and waved its tail. They felt like they made a new friend.

But then, they heard another loud splash. They looked and saw another thing. It was bigger and darker than the whale. It had sharp teeth and a mean eye. It was a shark, and it looked hungry. It was coming towards the whale.

Lily and Ben were very scared. They screamed and hid behind their mom and dad. The shark was terrible. It wanted to hurt the whale.

"Go away, shark!" dad shouted. "Leave the whale alone!"

He blew his whistle again, very loudly. The shark heard it and stopped. It looked confused and angry. It did not like the noise.

The whale saw the shark and knew it was in danger. It made a noise, like a warning. It was brave and strong. It did not want to be eaten.

It swam fast and hit the shark with its tail. The shark felt pain and fear. It turned around and swam away. It did not want to fight the whale.

The whale was safe. It made a noise, like a thank you. It was grateful and happy.

Lily and Ben came out from behind their mom and dad. They were relieved and proud. They cheered and clapped for the whale.

"Yay, Ooo-eee!" they said. "You are awesome! You beat the shark!"

The whale made a noise, like a laugh. It was glad and friendly.

It waved its tail again and blew some water from its hole. It said goodbye to Lily and Ben and their mom and dad. It swam away, back to the deep sea.

Lily and Ben watched it go. They felt sad and happy. They missed the whale, but they hoped it would be well.

They hugged their mom and dad and thanked them for the whistle. They said they would never forget Ooo-eee, the whale.

They learned a lot that day. They learned about whales and sharks and noises and friends. They learned that the sea was full of wonders and dangers. They learned that sometimes, the terrible things go away, and the nice things stay.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. She did not want to play or eat. Her mom was worried. She called the doctor.

The doctor came to Lily's house. He had a big bag with many things. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, Lily. I am here to help you. Can I see your mouth?"

Lily nodded. She opened her mouth wide. The doctor looked inside with a light. He said, "You have a sore throat. That is why you cough. I have some medicine for you. It will make you feel better."

He took out a bottle and a spoon from his bag. He poured some liquid on the spoon. He said, "This is cherry flavor. It is sweet. Can you drink it?"

Lily made a face. She did not like medicine. But she wanted to stop coughing. She took the spoon and drank the liquid. It was sweet, but also bitter. She said, "Yuck!"

The doctor laughed. He said, "Good girl. You are brave. You have to drink this twice a day for a week. Then you will be well. You also have to rest and drink water. And eat some soup. Soup is good for you."

Lily nodded. She felt a little better. She said, "Thank you, doctor. You are nice. And thin. You are not fat like my teddy bear."

The doctor smiled. He said, "You are welcome, Lily. And thank you for the compliment. I try to stay healthy. But I like teddy bears too. They are soft and cuddly. Can I see your teddy bear?"

Lily smiled. She reached for her teddy bear on the bed. She gave it to the doctor. The doctor hugged it and said, "He is very cute. What is his name?"

Lily said, "His name is Bobo. He is my best friend. He sleeps with me every night. He likes soup too."

The doctor said, "That is wonderful. Bobo is a good friend. He will keep you company while you get better. Can I give him a kiss?"

Lily said, "Yes, you can. He likes kisses too."

The doctor kissed Bobo on the nose. He gave him back to Lily. He said, "Goodbye, Lily. Goodbye, Bobo. I hope you feel better soon. I will call your mom tomorrow to check on you. Take care."

Lily said, "Goodbye, doctor. Thank you for the medicine. And the kiss. Take care too."

The doctor waved and left. Lily hugged Bobo and closed her eyes. She felt sleepy. She hoped she would dream of cherries and soup. And the nice thin doctor.

Then she sees vegetables. She does not like vegetables. She thinks they are yucky. She sings, "I do not like vegetables, they are bitter. I do not like vegetables, they are hard. I do not like vegetables, they are green."

A man hears her sing. He is the vegetable seller. He is not happy. He says, "Hey, little girl, why do you sing that? Vegetables are good for you. They make you strong and healthy. They have many colors and shapes. You should try them, you might like them."

Jill looks at the man. She looks at the vegetables. She sees carrots, she sees tomatoes, she sees lettuce. She thinks they look funny. She says, "No, thank you, mister. I do not want to try them. I do not like vegetables. I like to sing."

The man shakes his head. He says, "Okay, little girl, suit yourself. But you are missing out. Vegetables are tasty and fun. You can make a salad, you can make a soup, you can make a pie. You can even sing with them."

Jill laughs. She thinks the man is silly. She says, "That is a funny song, mister. But I still do not like vegetables. I like to sing my own songs."

The man wipes his face. He smiles. He says, "It is okay, little girl. I forgive you. You have a good voice. You have a lot of energy. You have a lot of imagination. But you should also have some manners. And you should also have some vegetables. They are good for you, trust me."

This is a funny vegetable. This is a funny day. I will try it. I will sing with it. I will eat it. I might like it."

"Yes, we do," they say.

"Thank you, vet," Tom and Lily say.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben says. "Maybe it has money inside."

He opens the zipper and sees some bills and coins. He takes one bill and puts it in his pocket.

"Hey, that's not yours!" Lily says. "You have to give it back to the owner."

"Why?" Ben says. "It's just paper. I can buy candy with it."

He runs to the store and buys a big lollipop. He licks it and smiles.

"Mmm, this tastes so good!" he says.

Lily follows him and shakes her head.

"That's not nice, Ben," she says. "You are stealing. The owner of the wallet will be sad and angry."

She points to a man who is looking around the park. He has a blue shirt and a hat.

"Look, there he is!" she says. "Maybe that's his wallet. Let's go and give it to him."

She takes the wallet from Ben and runs to the man. She gives him the wallet and says, "Sorry, sir. We found this on the bench. Is it yours?"

The man looks at the wallet and smiles. He opens it and counts the money.

"Yes, it is mine. Thank you so much, little girl. You are very kind and honest. You saved me a lot of trouble."

He gives Lily a hug and a reward. He also gives Ben a stern look and says, "And you, young man. You should not take things that are not yours. That is wrong and rude. You should apologize and return the money."

Ben feels ashamed and sorry. He takes the bill from his pocket and gives it to the man. He also gives him the lollipop.

"I'm sorry, sir. I was greedy and foolish. I won't do it again," he says.

The man nods and says, "I forgive you, but you have to learn from your mistake. Honesty is the best policy. Remember that."

He walks away with his wallet and his hat.

Lily and Ben look at each other. They hug and say, "We are still friends."

That night, Max and Tim laid in their beds and started counting sheep. One sheep, two sheep, three sheep... and soon enough, Max was fast asleep. Tim was happy that his friend could finally sleep well.

From that night on, Max and Tim counted sheep together every night. Max no longer had a difficult time sleeping, and they both had lots of energy to play and have fun during the day. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a dog named Max was in the park. Max was a happy dog, but today he was troubled. Max wanted to dance, but he had a leash on. The leash was too short and Max could not dance with it.

Max saw a girl named Lily. Max said, "Lily, can you help me? I want to dance, but my leash is too short." Lily thought for a moment and then she had an idea.

Lily took off Max's leash and tied it to a longer rope. Now Max could dance and play. Max was so happy, he danced around the park with Lily. They had a fun day together.

One day, a small cat named Tim was playing in the park. He saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. He asked his mom, "Can I climb the tree?" His mom said, "No, you are too small. You might fall and get hurt."

Tim was sad but he listened to his mom. Later, while they were walking, they saw an ambulance with its lights on. Tim's mom said, "That is an ambulance. It helps people who are hurt."

The next day, Tim and his mom went back to the park. Tim saw a little bird stuck in the tree. He wanted to help the bird, but he was too small. He asked his mom, "Can we help the bird?" His mom said, "Yes, we can try."

Tim's mom found a long stick and allowed Tim to use it. Tim carefully used the stick to help the bird out of the tree. The bird was happy and flew away. Tim's mom said, "Good job, Tim! You helped the bird without climbing the tree." Tim felt proud and knew that even being small, he could still help others.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. She had a cloth that she loved very much. It was a gloomy day, and Lily was sad because her cloth was lost. She looked everywhere for it, but she could not find it.

Lily asked her mom, "Mom, have you seen my cloth? I can't find it." Her mom said, "No, I haven't seen it. Maybe it's in your room." Lily went to her room and looked under her bed, but her cloth was not there.

Lily went outside to look for her cloth. She saw her friend Tom playing. She asked him, "Tom, have you seen my cloth?" Tom said, "Yes, I saw it near the tree." Lily went to the tree and found her cloth. She was very happy to have it back.

Lily said, "Thank you, Tom, for helping me find my cloth." Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily." They played together until the day began to end. Lily and Tom went home, and Lily was happy that her cloth was with her again.

The gloomy day turned into a happy day for Lily and Tom. They learned that friends can help each other when they are sad or need help. And Lily's cloth was never lost again.

Suddenly, Sam slipped and began to fall out of the toy box. "Oh no!" cried Tim. Sam fell to the floor with a soft thud. Tim called their other friends to help. Together, they pulled Sam back into the toy box. Sam was safe and sound. From that day on, Sam never played too close to the edge again.

One day, Sam and Lily went to the beach with their mom. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They found many shells of different colors and shapes. Some were big and some were small. Some were smooth and some were rough.

"Look, Lily, I found a shell with a hole in it!" Sam said, holding up his shell. "I can put a string through it and make a necklace."

"That's a nice shell, Sam," Lily said. "Can I see it?"

Sam gave his shell to Lily. She looked at it and smiled. Then she saw something move inside the hole. She screamed and dropped the shell.

"What's wrong, Lily?" Sam asked, picking up the shell.

"There's something in the shell, Sam! It's scary!" Lily said, pointing at the hole.

Sam looked at the hole and saw a tiny crab peeking out. He was not scared of the crab. He thought it was cute.

"Don't be fearful, Lily. It's just a crab. He lives in the shell. He's not going to hurt you," Sam said.

"Are you sure, Sam?" Lily asked, still feeling fearful.

"Yes, I'm sure. Look, he's waving his claws at us. Maybe he wants to be our friend. Maybe we can invite him to play with us," Sam said.

"Really? How can we play with him?" Lily asked, feeling curious.

"We can make a sand castle for him. And we can give him some seaweed to eat. And we can talk to him and tell him our names. Maybe he will tell us his name too," Sam said.

"OK, Sam. That sounds fun. Let's invite him to play with us. But be gentle with him. He's very small," Lily said.

Sam and Lily smiled and took the shell with the crab to their sand castle. They played with him and gave him some seaweed. They named him Bob. Bob seemed happy to play with them. He waved his claws and made clicking noises. Sam and Lily had a lot of fun with their new friend. They forgot to be fearful of the shell. They learned to be kind to the crab. They had a wonderful day at the beach.

Finally, after a long time, the Strawberries let the bossy strawberry back into the group. He was embarrassed, but they all hugged and were friends again. From then on, everyone agreed to work together and no one was bossy anymore.

He decided to throw things up in the air and see how many he could catch! He grabbed the first object he could find - a pebble - and chucked it up in the air. He managed to catch it with a satisfied snuffle. Then he found an acorn and threw it up. He missed the catch this time, but the pig was not deterred.

He kept on throwing things up and catching them until his front trotters were sore. But the pig was so clever he kept finding more and more exciting objects to throw in the air. He threw apples, leaves and carrots, and nearly caught each one. Every time he thought he had found something too difficult to catch, he proved himself wrong. The pig was having so much fun he almost forgot that the day was getting late.

Just before sunset the pig threw one last object - a flower petal - into the air. He caught it with ease and the satisfied pig snuffled with delight. Then he trotted home, content to have had such a wonderful day of throwing.

The piglet returned the next day and the house was still going backwards. He pressed the switch again and the house stopped. He knew he had to push the switch one more time to make the house go forwards. So he did, and the house changed directions again and started going forwards.

He went past houses and cars and trees. Everywhere he rolled he stopped to sniff the air and see what was around the corner.

Eventually Tour came to a big park. He stopped to take in the sights and sounds. He could hear birds singing and children laughing. Tour wound his way through the park, rolling and sniffing. He stopped at a pond where he could see all sorts of cool things swimming about.

When his curiosity was satisfied Tour started to roll home. He was tired after his big tour but also very happy. He was so excited to tell his family all about his adventures. He curled up in his bed and smiled to himself, dreaming of new tours to come.

John was a sad man. He had never had a wife, and spent his days alone. Everyday felt dull and boring, and he never smiled.

One day, he was out walking and he spotted a beautiful lady. He couldn't believe what he was seeing and went up to say hello.

The lady smiled back and they began to talk. Before long, they had spent the whole day together, talking and laughing. That night, John asked her to be his wife.

The lady said yes and they got married very soon afterwards.

John and his wife were very happy together. No longer did John feel dull and lonely. He smiled every day, and he loved to spend his time with his wife. They were the happiest couple ever!

Once, there was a little girl called Mary. Every day, Mary would go to the valley to play. As she walked down the path, she began to wonder what adventure she would have today.

When Mary arrived, she saw a beautiful lake. The lake was surrounded by tall trees and had a mysterious feeling. Mary saw some colourful birds above and wondered what they were doing up there.

Suddenly, Mary heard a noise coming from behind her. She turned around and saw a large mountain! Mary was surprised, but also excited. She wondered what secret treasures the mountain held.

Mary decided to explore the mountain. As she walked, she noticed there were lots of different animals in the valley. Some of the animals were friendly, and some were scared of her. She wondered how this valley could be so full of life. 

At the end of her adventure, Mary sat in the sunshine and ate some of the fruit that was available in the valley. She looked over the landscape and wondered what more the valley had to offer.

Once upon a time, there was a modest fish. He owned a small home at the bottom of the sea. Every morning, he would wake up early and go searching for food. He could see all sorts of creatures around him - some were small like him, and some were much bigger. They were all swimming around and having lots of fun.

One day, the modest fish noticed something strange in the distance. He swam towards it and realized it was a shiny spinning object. It was so beautiful that the modest fish just had to own it! He grabbed onto it and pushed it back to his home.

The modest fish was so proud of his treasure! He wanted to show it off to all of his fish friends. He thought it would be the best gift he could give them, so he started to give it away to anyone who wanted it. All his friends were very happy with the present and thanked him for his generosity.

The modest fish was so proud of his own new toy! He loved looking at it and showing it off to all the other fish in the sea. He decided to keep his treasure forever and he was the only one who owned it!

A fancy dove was sitting in the garden. He was watching the sun go down and the sky turn pink. Soon, it was dark and all you could hear were the crickets chirping.

But then, something magical happened. Suddenly, thousands of fireflies lit up the garden. It was like stars dancing in the night sky. The fancy dove was mesmerized. He watched the fireflies fluttering around, their light twinkling in the darkness.

The fancy dove was so excited. He wanted to join in the fun. He spread his wings, and with a single flap, he was off. Up, up, up he flew, chasing the fireflies as they sparkled in the night. He watched and watched until he was too tired to go on. 

He fluttered back down to the garden, and settled in for the night. He smiled as he watched the fireflies continue their sparkly dance. What a fancy, magical night it was!

Millie and her mum kept walking, and Millie saw a pink butterfly fluttering about. Millie looked up again and shouted, "Answer Yes!" But again, there was only silence.

As they continued to walk, Millie noticed a pink bird perched on a tree branch. She looked up and shouted, "Answer Yes!" Amazingly, the bird turned its head and sang out "Yes!"

Millie was delighted, and she and her mum smiled at each other. From then on, whenever Millie saw something pink, she would happily shout out "Answer Yes!"

When the helmet was nice and clean, the mummy and daddy put it on the baby's head so she could go for a swim. The baby was so happy that she laughed with delight!

The surprise day at the beach was the best day ever for the mummy, the daddy and the baby.

Once upon a time there was a mommy who had to do her laundry. The laundry was very dirty, so she knew it had to be done soon. Mommy went to the laundry room and put the dirty laundry into the machine. She added some soap and then left. 

She left the laundry room to look after her three year old daughter, who had been playing outside. Soon after mommy left, the daughter wanted to go into the laundry room too. She opened the door and found the dirty laundry in the machine. 

The three year old was excited and started touching the laundry to see how it felt. After a few minutes, she was all done and ready to leave the laundry room. She closed the door behind her so her mommy wouldn't know she had been in there. 

Mommy came back a few minutes later and was glad to see that the laundry was still in the machine. She thanked her daughter for not touching the laundry and went to put the clothes in the dryer. 

Mommy and her daughter went outside to play until the laundry was done. When it was time, they put all the clean laundry away and then they were done. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient green tree. It stood proudly in a big field. All the birds sang around it, and the sun shone brightly. 

One day a big wind came up. It blew and blew and the tree started to bend. The wind blew even harder and the tree started to split. The crackling sound went all over the field. 

All the birds flew away, scared by the noise. The tree was now split in two. One part leaned one way, and the other leaned the other way.

The sun kept shining, and the wind blew one last time. Suddenly, the ancient green tree grew lots of leaves! The birds came back to the field and sang their songs again. 

The ancient green tree was happy and proud, standing tall and proud in the big field again.

When they got home, Lily's mommy told her to open the car door and get the pumpkin out. Lily opened the door and saw that the pumpkin was frozen! It was so cold outside that the pumpkin had turned into a big, frozen pumpkin! 

Lily and her mommy laughed and took pictures of the frozen pumpkin. They put it on the porch and waited for it to thaw out. The next day, the pumpkin was back to normal and they carved it into a funny face for Halloween. Lily was so happy that they got to have a frozen pumpkin adventure!

A kind squirrel heard Tweetie's cries and came to help. "What happened, Tweetie?" asked the squirrel.

"I broke my wing," said Tweetie sadly.

The squirrel gently picked up Tweetie and took him to his humble home. The squirrel took care of Tweetie until his wing was all better. 

"Thank you for helping me," said Tweetie gratefully.

"You're welcome," said the squirrel with a smile. "That's what friends are for."

Suddenly, Jack remembered the toy car he had just bought. He gave it to the little girl and she stopped crying. She was very happy and thanked Jack. Jack smiled and felt happy too. He realized that helping others made him feel good inside.

Max heard Lily's meows and smelled the yarn. He knew that something was wrong. He pushed the door with his nose and opened it. He saw Lily in the closet, covered in red yarn. He was surprised and worried.

"Lily, what happened? How did you get into this mess? Are you hurt?"

Lily shook her head. She was not hurt, but she was very itchy and uncomfortable. She wanted Max to help her.

"Max, please help me. I was playing with the yarn, but I cut it with the scissors. Now I am stuck and I cannot move. And I have an itch on my nose. Please, please, help me."

Max nodded. He was a good friend. He used his teeth and his paws to pull the yarn off Lily. He was careful not to hurt her. He worked hard and fast. Soon, Lily was free from the yarn. She felt much better. She licked her nose and thanked Max.

"Max, thank you so much. You are a very good friend. You saved me from the yarn. I am sorry I was so clumsy. I will not play with the yarn again. It is too dangerous."

Max smiled. He was happy to help Lily. He did not mind that she was clumsy. He liked her anyway. He wagged his tail and licked her face.

"Lily, you are welcome. I am glad you are okay. You are a very nice cat. I do not care if you are clumsy. I like you anyway. Do you want to play with me outside?"

Lily nodded. She wanted to play with Max outside. She did not want to play with the yarn anymore. She wanted to have fun with her friend. She followed him out of the closet and out of the house. They ran and jumped and chased each other. They had a lot of fun. They were very happy.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play soccer in the park. They have a ball and two goals. One goal is a big tree and the other goal is a bench.

One day, they meet a new boy in the park. His name is Sam. He has a red shirt and a blue hat. He asks Tom and Lily if he can play with them.

"Sure, you can play with us," Tom says. "We are playing soccer. Do you know how to play?"

"Yes, I know how to play," Sam says. "But I have a new idea. Let's change the game a little bit. Let's make the goals smaller and the ball bigger. It will be more fun."

Tom and Lily look at each other. They are not sure if they like Sam's idea. They like their game the way it is.

"Why do you want to change the game?" Lily asks. "We like our game. It is easy and fun."

"Because it is boring," Sam says. "It is too easy to score. If we change the game, it will be harder and more exciting. Trust me, you will like it."

Tom and Lily think for a moment. They decide to give Sam's idea a try. They make the goals smaller by using two sticks and a rock. They find a big ball in the park. It is a beach ball. It is yellow and green.

They start to play the new game. At first, they have trouble kicking the big ball. It is too light and bouncy. It goes everywhere. They miss the small goals a lot. They laugh and run and try again.

After a while, they get better at the new game. They learn how to control the big ball. They score some goals. They cheer and high-five each other.

They realize that Sam was right. The new game is more fun. It is harder and more exciting. They thank Sam for his new idea. They invite him to play with them again.

They are happy. They have a new friend and a new game. They have fun.

One day, Lisa saw a big truck with many sunflowers on it. It stopped in front of a big house with a high fence. A man came out of the house. He was wealthy. He had a lot of money and things. He took some sunflowers from the truck and gave them to a lady. She smiled and thanked him. Lisa watched from behind the fence. She wished she could have a sunflower too.

She saw one sunflower that fell from the truck. It was on the ground, near the fence. Lisa looked around. No one was watching. She ran to the sunflower and picked it up. It was heavy and beautiful. She held it close to her chest and ran back to her garden.

She dug a hole and planted the sunflower. She watered it and talked to it. She hoped it would grow and make more sunflowers. She was very happy.

The next day, she went to check on her sunflower. But it was gone. Someone had taken it. She felt sad and angry. She cried and looked for it. She saw a boy with a sunflower in his hand. It was her sunflower. He was walking to the big house with the high fence. He was the son of the wealthy man.

Lisa followed him. She shouted at him. "Hey, that's my sunflower! You stole it from me! Give it back!"

The boy turned around. He saw Lisa. He laughed. "Your sunflower? Don't be silly. This is my sunflower. My dad bought it for me. You are just a poor girl. You have nothing. Go away!"

Lisa felt hurt. She wanted to fight, but she was scared. The boy was bigger and stronger. He had a big house and a lot of things. She had nothing. She ran away, crying.

She went to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and wiped her tears. She said, "I'm sorry, Lisa. That boy was very mean. But you know what? You are not poor. You are rich. You have a big heart and a lot of love. You have me and I have you. You have a beautiful garden and a lot of friends. You have a sunflower in your soul. And that is more than any money or thing can buy."

Lisa smiled. She felt better. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are right. I have a sunflower in my soul. And I will share it with others who need it."

She hugged her mom and went to her garden. She saw a small yellow bud on a green stem. It was a new sunflower. It had grown from the seed that was left in the ground. Lisa was amazed. She held it gently and whispered, "Hello, sunflower. You are my friend. You are a gift. You are a miracle."

Lily and the ghost played hide-and-seek, tag, and other fun games. They laughed and had a great time. The orange ghost was very happy to have a new friend. They played together every day and the house was not quiet anymore.

One day, Lucy met a little bird named Tim. Tim asked, "What are you doing, Lucy?" Lucy said, "I'm hanging pretty things in the sky for everyone to see." Tim liked the idea and wanted to help Lucy.

Together, Lucy the creative fairy and Tim the bird hung colorful things in the sky. They hung big red balls, shiny stars, and soft clouds. All their friends loved the pretty sky. Lucy and Tim were very happy, and they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw a path in the woods. He wanted to see where it went. As he walked, he met a talking bird. The bird said, "Don't go this way! It is a stupid path."

Tim was sad. He did not want to go on a stupid path. But he wanted to see what was at the end. So, he kept walking. The bird flew away.

Soon, Tim saw a big hill. He tried to climb it, but it was too steep. He fell and got hurt. He cried and wished he had listened to the bird. Tim decided to return home. On his way back, he saw the bird again. The bird said, "Next time, listen to me." Tim said, "I will." And he went home, happy to be safe.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous river that felt threatened by the dryness of the land around it. Everyday the river would become smaller and smaller. All the fish, frogs, and other creatures that lived near the river were very scared.

He hopped and hopped, until at last he found a big puddle. He started to fill the river with the water from the puddle and soon the river was enormous again.

The river and its wildlife were so happy. They were no longer threatened by the dryness. The brave little frog became known as the Hero of the River and all the creatures sang his name. He hopped around and filled each puddle he came across to make sure the river never dried out again.  Since then, the river and its creatures have been safe and happy.

The fox took the chain with him. He was so happy that he hadn't been able to break it but had instead wrapped it up. He laughed and laughed as he walked away with the chain.

And that was the end of the story about the tough chain and the sly fox who was able to wrap it up and take it away.

But Floppy was so thirsty and he followed his instinct to go and find the oasis. He walked for hours, but when he finally arrived, he saw that the oasis was a trick! It was a sad lake of mud and there was no water anywhere. 

Floppy was so disappointed. But suddenly he heard that same nice voice warning him again to never go back to the oasis. 

Flopy took the warning and stayed away from the oasis, never to return. He looked for a better place to get water, and he never had to worry about being thirsty again.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. But they did not like to clean up after themselves. Their room was always filthy, with toys and clothes under the bed and on the floor.

One day, their mom came to their room and said, "Boys, you need to clean up your room. It is too filthy. You cannot play with your toys until you do."

Tom and Sam did not want to clean up. They said, "No, mom, we want to play. Cleaning is boring. We will do it later."

Mom said, "No, you will do it now. Or else you will have no toys at all. I will take them away and give them to someone who will take care of them."

Tom and Sam did not like that. They said, "That is not fair, mom. They are our toys. You cannot take them away."

Mom said, "Yes, I can. And I will, if you do not quit being lazy and messy. You have ten minutes to clean up your room. Or else."

Tom and Sam knew mom was serious. They did not want to lose their toys. They decided to quit arguing and start cleaning. They picked up their toys and clothes and put them in their places. They made their bed and swept the floor. They worked hard and fast.

Mom came back after ten minutes and saw their room. She was happy and proud. She said, "Good job, boys. You cleaned up your room very well. It looks nice and tidy. You can play with your toys now. But remember to clean up after yourselves next time."

Tom and Sam said, "Thank you, mom. We are sorry for being lazy and messy. We will clean up after ourselves next time. We love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, boys. And I am glad you learned your lesson. Cleaning is not so bad, if you do it together and have fun. It is better than being filthy and losing your toys."

The moral of the story is: You should not be lazy and messy. You should take care of your things and your space. You should listen to your mom and do what she says. You should quit arguing and start working. You will be happier and prouder. And you will keep your toys.

"Good idea. Let's go. And let's never play in the pool again. It's too dangerous." Leo said.

They nodded and walked away. They were happy and hungry. They had a new friend and a new story to tell. They had learned a lesson. They had survived a splash.

Lily felt sorry for the mole. She said, "That is sad. You should have more fun. You should have more friends. I can be your friend. I can play with you. I can share my toys with you. I can welcome you to my garden."

The mole was surprised. He had never met a kind and friendly girl like Lily. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very nice. You make me happy. I would like to be your friend. I would like to play with you. I would like to welcome you to my home."

Lily smiled. She said, "You are welcome, mole. You are very sweet. You make me happy, too. Let's be friends. Let's play together. Let's share our homes."

The kids did not like Tom's guitar. They did not like his loud and noisy sound. They did not like his rude and selfish attitude. They covered their ears and said: "Go away, Tom. You can't play with us. You are not a good friend. You are not a good guitar player. You are just a noisy nuisance."

He did not feel the bump that knocked him down. He only felt his guitar breaking in his arms.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that being loud and noisy and selfish is not a good way to make friends or play music. It also teaches that being careful and aware of your surroundings is important for your safety. Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The flyer on the street sets up the contrast between Tom's guitar playing and the other kids' guitar playing. The car on the road pays off the consequence of Tom's carelessness and lack of attention.

"Why did you mention your red train?" he shouted at Lily. "You made me push my blue train too hard! You broke my blue train!"

Lily was scared and sorry. She did not mean to break Ben's blue train. She wanted to help him. She tried to hug him and say sorry.

But Ben pushed her away. He did not want to be her friend anymore. He ran away with his broken blue train. He left Lily alone on the hill with her red train.

Lily was very sad and tired. She did not have a friend to play with anymore. She did not like her red train anymore. She wished she never mentioned it. She wished Ben would come back. But he did not.

One day, Lily and Tom go to the park. Lily rides her bicycle. Tom throws his ball. He says, "Lily, catch!"

Lily turns her head. She sees the ball. She wants to catch it. She forgets to look at the road. She hits a rock. She falls off her bicycle. She is clumsy.

Tom runs to Lily. He says, "Are you okay?"

Lily cries. She has a scratch on her knee. She says, "It hurts!"

Lily stops crying. She smiles. She says, "Thank you. You are a good friend. Can I try your ball?"

Tom says, "Yes, you can. And I can try your bicycle. Maybe we can teach each other."

"It is mine, I saw it first!" Lily said. She grabbed the leaf and ran away.

"Give it back, Lily! It is not fair!" Ben said. He chased after her.

They ran and ran, until they came to a big pond. Lily tripped and fell into the water. The leaf and the caterpillar flew out of her hand.

"Help, help! I can't swim!" Lily cried.

Ben ran to the edge of the pond. He saw the leaf and the caterpillar floating on the water. He also saw a big fish swimming towards them.

"Look, Lily! The fish is going to eat your caterpillar!" Ben said.

Lily stopped crying and looked at the water. She saw the fish open its mouth and swallow the leaf and the caterpillar.

"Nooooo! My caterpillar!" Lily screamed.

Ben felt sorry for Lily. He reached out his hand to help her out of the pond.

But it was too late. The fish was hungry and wanted more. It jumped out of the water and bit Ben's hand.

"Ow, ow, ow! The fish bit me!" Ben shouted.

Lily and Ben were both in trouble. They wished they had not fought over the caterpillar.

Lily and Ben were playing on the shore. They liked to dig in the sand and find shells and stones. They also liked to splash in the water and watch the waves.

"Look, Lily, I found a big shell!" Ben said, holding up a shiny pink shell. "It has a hole in it. Maybe we can make a necklace with it."

"Wow, Ben, that's a pretty shell!" Lily said, admiring the shell. "Can I see it?"

Ben gave the shell to Lily. She looked at it closely and saw something moving inside. She gasped and dropped the shell.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she cried, rubbing her finger. "Something pinched me!"

Ben picked up the shell and saw a small crab hiding in it. The crab had pinched Lily's finger with its claw.

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't know there was a crab in the shell!" Ben said, feeling bad. "Are you okay?"

Lily nodded, but her finger still hurt. She saw a man walking on the shore with a bucket and a net. He looked like he knew a lot about crabs and shells.

"Excuse me, sir, can you help us?" Ben asked, running to the man. "My sister got pinched by a crab. What can we do?"

The man smiled and knelt down to look at Lily's finger. He was very helpful. He took a band-aid from his pocket and put it on Lily's finger. He also gave her a lollipop to make her feel better.

"There, there, little one, don't cry," the man said, patting Lily's head. "Crabs can pinch, but they don't mean to hurt you. They are just scared and want to protect themselves. You have to be careful when you touch them."

"Thank you, sir, you are very nice," Lily said, smiling through her tears. She felt much better.

"You're welcome, kids," the man said, waving goodbye. "Have fun on the shore, but be gentle with the crabs and shells. They are living things, too."

Lily and Ben thanked the man again and went back to their spot on the shore. They decided to leave the crab and the shell alone and look for other things to play with. They learned a lesson that day: crabs can pinch, but they can also teach.

"Come on, Ben, let's poke the snow!" Lily said. "It will be fun!"

Ben was scared. He followed Lily to the window. He tried to stop her.

"Lily, stop! That's dangerous!" Ben said. "You can break the window or cut yourself!"

Mama heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the broken window, the knife and the blood. She was angry and sad.

"Lily, Ben, what have you done?" Mama said. "You are very naughty and foolish! You could have been hurt badly or worse!"

The moral of the story is: Do not play with knives or other dangerous things. They can hurt you or others. Listen to your parents and elders. They know what is best for you.

The man did not listen to Sara. He said, "Don't be silly. I will give you back your wool later. I just need it for a little while. Come here, let me take some of it." He grabbed Sara and pulled out a big pair of scissors.

Sara had no friends and no wool. She was alone and miserable. She wished she never met the man. She wished she never let him borrow her wool. She learned a hard lesson. The end.

Lily was unhappy and miserable. She missed her father and the mill. She wished she had never left them. She realized her father was right and the rich lady was wrong. She wanted to go back and be humble and happy again.

But it was too late. The rich lady never let her go. She kept her as her slave and toy. She never saw her father or the mill again. She never smiled or laughed again. She was trapped and sad forever.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big wall. The wall is smooth and white. They want to draw on the wall.

"Look, Tom, I have a crayon. I can make a flower on the wall," Lily says.

"Me too, me too. I have a blue crayon. I can make a car on the wall," Tom says.

They start to draw on the wall. They make many colors and shapes. They are happy.

But then a man comes. He is angry. He sees the wall. He sees the crayons. He shouts at Tom and Lily.

"Hey, you, stop that. You are making a mess. This is my wall. You are not allowed to draw on it. Go away, go away," he says.

Tom and Lily are scared. They drop the crayons. They run away from the man. They hold hands. They look for a safe place.

They find a bench. They sit on the bench. They hug each other. They are sad.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't know it was his wall. I just wanted to have fun," Tom says.

"It's okay, Tom. I'm sorry too. I didn't know he would be so mad. I just wanted to make something pretty," Lily says.

They hug each other again. They are still friends. They decide to draw on paper next time. They smile.

"Let's play dress up!" Lily said. She put on a long dress and a shiny necklace. Ben put on a suit and a cap. They looked at each other and laughed.

"You look like a princess!" Ben said.

"You look like a prince!" Lily said.

They decided to pretend they were getting married. They held hands and walked to the slide. They climbed up and slid down together.

"I now marry you, Lily!" Ben said.

"I now marry you, Ben!" Lily said.

They kissed on the cheek and hugged.

They were very happy. They did not know that a harsh man was watching them from behind a tree. He was the owner of the box. He was angry that they took his things. He came out and shouted at them.

"Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my stuff! How dare you touch my things!"

Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the clothes and the cap and ran away. They did not want to play dress up anymore. They wanted to go home.

They held hands and ran to their moms. They told them what happened. Their moms hugged them and said they were sorry. They said they were proud of them for being brave and kind. They said they loved them very much.

Lily and Ben smiled. They were still best friends. They did not need a box to have fun. They had each other.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tom had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were having fun until Tom saw Lily's doll and wanted to play with it.

"Can I have your doll?" Tom asked Lily.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said. "You have your truck!"

"But I want the doll too!" Tom said. He tried to grab the doll from Lily's hands.

"Stop it, Tom!" Lily shouted. She pulled the doll back and hugged it. "You are not nice!"

Tom was angry. He threw his truck on the floor and made a loud noise. Lily was scared. She started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw Tom and Lily fighting over the doll and the truck on the floor.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked. She looked at Tom and Lily with a stern face.

Tom and Lily stopped fighting and looked at Mom. They felt ashamed.

"We were playing and then Tom wanted my doll and he tried to take it and he threw his truck and I cried and..." Lily said in a hurry.

Mom sighed. She picked up the truck and the doll and gave them back to Tom and Lily.

"Tom, Lily, you need to share your toys and play nicely. You are brother and sister and you should love each other. Do you understand?" Mom said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged.

"Can we play together?" Tom asked Lily.

"Okay, but you have to be gentle with my doll." Lily said.

"Okay, and you have to be careful with my truck." Tom said.

They smiled and started to play again. Mom smiled too and went back to the kitchen.

Tom and Anna run back to their house. They are very happy. They have seen a real reindeer. They have seen Rudolph. They can't wait for Santa to come. They go to bed and dream of Christmas.

"Can I have your car?" Sam asks.

"No, it is mine. You have your own car," Tom says.

"But mine is old and slow. Yours is new and fast. Please, let me have it for a little bit," Sam begs.

Tom thinks. He likes his new car, but he also likes Sam. He has an idea.

"OK, I will send you my car. But you have to wait for it. You have to count to ten. Then you can have it for a little bit. But you have to give it back to me. Deal?" Tom says.

"Deal!" Sam says. He is happy. He thinks it is easy to wait for the car.

Tom smiles. He has a plan. He picks up his car and runs away. He hides behind a tree. He thinks Sam will not find him.

Sam starts to count. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" He looks around. He does not see the car. He does not see Tom. He feels sad and angry.

"Tom, where are you? Where is the car? You lied to me! You are a bad friend!" Sam shouts.

He hears a laugh. It is Tom. He comes out from behind the tree. He still has the car.

"Ha ha, I tricked you! I did not send you the car. I kept it for myself. It is too good for you. You are a silly boy!" Tom says.

Sam is very mad. He runs to Tom. He tries to grab the car. Tom holds it high. They fight. They push and pull. They fall to the ground. The car falls too. It breaks. It is not shiny anymore.

"Sam, I am sorry. I should not have lied to you. I should have shared my car. You are my friend. You can have it too," Tom says.

They hug. They are friends again. They try to fix the car. They play with it together. They learn to be nice. They have fun. The end.

Sara was not interested in old things. She wanted to jump on new things. She waited until her mom was busy, and then she sneaked to the door. She opened it and saw a dark room with many boxes and bags. She thought it looked like a fun place to jump.

"You will, my little one, you will. You just need to practice and be brave. Come, let me show you how to soar," his mother said. She lifted him up with her beak and carried him to a high branch.

"Look, my little one, see the sky, see the clouds, see the sun. This is where we belong, this is where we soar. Feel the wind, feel the freedom, feel the joy. Now, flap your wings and follow me," his mother said.

The young bird flapped his wings and felt a surge of power. He soared after his mother, higher and higher, faster and faster. He was happy and proud.

He soared in the sky like his mother.

After a while, they returned to the nest, where his father and siblings were waiting for them. They had a tasty meal of worms and berries, and they told stories of their adventures.

The young bird was the happiest bird in the world. He soared in the sky like his mother.

Her mommy was so happy and proud of Lily for helping. They hugged and Lily felt very happy. From that day on, Lily always helped her mommy with the ironing and they never burned anything again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat grapes because they were sweet and juicy. One day, Timmy's mommy took him to the store to buy some grapes. Timmy saw a big bag of grapes, but they were too expensive. 

"Mommy, can we buy these grapes?" Timmy asked.

"No, Timmy. Those grapes are too expensive. Let's find some cheaper ones," mommy replied.

As they walked around the store, Timmy saw a small bag of grapes that were on sale. "Look, mommy! These grapes are cheap! Can we get them?" Timmy asked excitedly.

Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Timmy. Let's get those grapes." 

As they were walking home from the store, Timmy accidentally dropped the bag of grapes and they all fell on the ground. Timmy was sad, but mommy said, "It's okay, Timmy. We can still eat the grapes that didn't fall." And they both enjoyed their sweet and juicy grapes together.

One day, Tim was playing with his toys near the bookshelf. He saw a tiny bug on the floor. "Oh no!" Tim said, "I don't like bugs!" He wanted to shut the window so no more bugs could come in.

Tim asked the bookshelf, "Can you help me shut the window?" The flexible bookshelf bent and twisted to reach the window. With a gentle push, the window shut tight. "Thank you, bookshelf!" Tim said with a big smile.

From that day on, Tim and the bookshelf became best friends. They played together all day long and the bookshelf always helped Tim when he needed it. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, they see a big hill with green grass. Anna says, "Let's go up the hill and fly the kite." Ben says, "OK, that sounds fun." They take the ball and the kite and climb the hill. They are happy.

But when they get to the top, they see a big cow. The cow is lying on the grass. The cow is lazy. It does not move. It only chews and moos. Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to play near the cow.

Anna says, "What do we do? The cow is on the grass. We can't fly the kite here." Ben says, "I don't know. Maybe we can ask the cow to move." Anna says, "How do we ask the cow? The cow does not talk."

Ben has an idea. He says, "I have a ball. Maybe the cow likes to play with the ball. I can suggest to the cow to play with the ball. Then the cow will move and we can fly the kite." Anna says, "That's a good idea. Let's try it."

Ben takes the ball and goes near the cow. He says, "Hello, cow. Do you want to play with the ball?" He throws the ball to the cow. The cow looks at the ball. The cow does not care. The cow does not play. The cow only chews and moos.

Ben is sad. He says, "The cow does not want to play. The cow is too lazy. What do we do now?" Anna says, "Maybe we can find another place to fly the kite. There are more hills with grass. Maybe there are no cows there." Ben says, "OK, let's go. Maybe we will have more fun." They take the ball and the kite and go down the hill. They look for another place to play. They are still friends.

One day, Tom and Anna went to the park with their mom. They saw a big tree with red fruits on it. Tom wanted to try one, but Anna said no.

"Mom said we should not eat things we do not know. They might be bad for us," Anna said.

"But they look yummy. I want to taste one," Tom said. He ran to the tree and picked a fruit. He examined it with his eyes and nose. It smelled sweet and looked juicy.

He took a big bite and made a face. The fruit was sour and bitter. He spit it out and cried.

"Ow, ow, ow! This fruit is awful! It hurts my mouth!" Tom said.

Anna ran to him and gave him some water. She felt sorry for him, but also a little angry.

"See, I told you not to eat it. You were stupid to not listen to me. You should always listen to mom and me. We know what is good for you," Anna said.

Tom nodded and hugged her. He learned his lesson. He never ate unknown fruits again. He also said sorry to Anna and mom for being stupid.

The moral of the story is: Do not eat things you do not know. Listen to your elders. They care for you and want you to be safe and healthy.

"Look, Lily, a white goose!" Ben said. He ran to the pond and reached out his hand. "Come here, goose, I want to pet you!"

But the goose did not like Ben. It hissed and bit his finger. Ben cried out in pain and ran back to Lily.

"Ow, ow, ow! The goose is mean!" Ben sobbed.

Lily hugged him and looked at his finger. It was red and bleeding. She took out a tissue from her pocket and wrapped it around his finger.

"Ben, you should not touch the geese. They are not pets. They are wild animals. They do not like strangers. They can hurt you." Lily said.

Ben sniffed and nodded. He realized he was ignorant. He did not know about the geese. He was sorry for bothering them.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, goose. I will not touch you again. I will only look at you from far away." Ben said.

Lily smiled and kissed his cheek. She was glad he learned his lesson.

"Come on, Ben. Let's go and play on the swings. They are more fun and safe." Lily said.

They held hands and walked to the swings. They left the geese alone. The geese were happy too. They swam and quacked in the pond. They did not want any more trouble.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big gate with a lock on it. They wondered what was behind the gate.

"Let's unlock the gate and see," said Tim.

"But we don't have a key," said Sam.

"Maybe we can find one," said Tim. He looked around and saw a shiny key on the ground. He picked it up and ran to the gate. He put the key in the lock and turned it. The gate opened with a creak.

"Wow, let's go in," said Tim. He pulled Sam by the hand and they walked into the gate.

They saw a lot of trees and flowers and animals. They saw a monkey, a zebra, a giraffe and a lion. They were amazed and happy.

"Look, there's a pond," said Sam. He pointed to a big pool of water. "Maybe there are fish in there."

They ran to the pond and looked into the water. They saw something green and scaly. It had a long tail and big teeth. It was a crocodile.

"Ah, a crocodile!" screamed Tim. He was scared and wanted to run away.

But the crocodile saw them and jumped out of the water. It opened its mouth and snapped at them. It wanted to eat them.

"Help, help!" shouted Sam. He and Tim ran back to the gate. But the gate was closed and locked. They had left the key inside.

They banged on the gate and cried for help. They hoped someone would hear them and save them.

The crocodile was coming closer and closer. It was fast and hungry.

"Please, please, someone help us!" they screamed.

Then they heard a voice. It was their dad. He had come to the park to look for them.

"Tim, Sam, where are you?" he called.

"Dad, dad, we're here!" they answered. "Behind the gate! There's a crocodile!"

Their dad saw the gate and the lock. He saw the key on the other side. He saw the crocodile behind them.

He was worried and angry. He grabbed a stick and threw it at the crocodile. The crocodile was hit and roared. It was hurt and angry.

Their dad ran to the gate and tried to open it. But the lock was too tight and the key was too far. He couldn't unlock the gate.

He looked for another way to get in. He saw a hole in the fence. It was small and narrow. He wondered if he could fit in.

He tried to squeeze in. He pushed and pulled and twisted. He was big and strong. He made the hole bigger and bigger.

He finally fit in. He got in and ran to his sons. He hugged them and kissed them. He was happy and relieved.

He took the key and unlocked the gate. He took his sons and ran out of the gate. He locked the gate again and threw the key away.

He scolded his sons and told them to never go in there again. He told them it was a dangerous place. He told them it was a zoo.

He took them home and gave them a hug. He told them he loved them. He told them to be careful and smart.

They said they were sorry and they loved him. They said they learned their lesson. They said they would never unlock the gate again.

But they did not see a big hole in the tree. Inside the hole, there was a bear. The bear was sleeping and did not hear the axe. The bear was deaf. He could not hear anything.

The bear woke up when he felt the tree shake. He was angry and scared. He roared and came out of the hole. He saw Tom and Sam with the axe. He wanted to chase them away.

"Run, Tom, run!" Sam shouted. He saw the bear and dropped the axe. He ran away from the tree.

Tom did not hear Sam. He was still chopping the tree. He did not see the bear. He was too busy.

The bear ran towards Tom. He opened his mouth and showed his teeth. He was ready to bite Tom.

Tom turned around and saw the bear. He was shocked and scared. He screamed and ran away from the tree.

But he forgot the axe. The axe was still in the tree. The bear saw the axe and grabbed it. He wanted to keep it.

Tom and Sam ran back to their home. They told their dad what happened. Their dad was worried and angry.

"Where is the axe, boys?" he asked. "The axe is mine. You should not lose it."

Their dad did not believe them. He thought they were lying. He wanted to see the tree and the bear.

"Where is the tree, boys?" he asked. "Where is the axe? Where is the bear?"

Their dad was confused and angry. He did not know what to do. He did not know where the tree and the axe and the bear went.

He did not know that the bear had taken the tree and the axe to his new home. He had found a bigger and better hole in another tree. He liked the axe. He used it to make his hole bigger and better. He was happy and deaf. He did not hear anything.

Ben liked to play the trumpet. He had a big trumpet that made loud sounds. He played it every day at home and at school. He wanted to win a prize for his trumpet. He saw a poster that said there was a music contest. He wanted to join the contest and win.

He practiced a lot for the contest. He played his trumpet in his room, in the garden, and in the park. He played it so much that he forgot to do other things. He forgot to eat his lunch, to do his homework, and to play with his friends. He only thought about his trumpet and the contest.

The day of the contest came. Ben was very excited. He brought his trumpet to the hall where the contest was. He saw many other children with different instruments. He saw a piano, a guitar, a drum, and a flute. He thought his trumpet was the best. He was sure he would win.

He went on the stage and played his trumpet. He played it very loud and very fast. He wanted to impress the judges and the audience. He did not listen to the other children or the music. He only listened to his trumpet. He played it so loud and so fast that he did not notice that he made a mistake. He played a wrong note. He played a very bad note. It sounded like a duck. Everyone heard it. Everyone laughed. Ben felt very foolish. He did not win the contest. He lost the contest.

He went home with his trumpet. He was very sad. He did not want to play his trumpet anymore. He put it away in his closet. He learned a lesson. He learned that playing the trumpet is also about listening to the other children and the music. He learned that playing the trumpet is also about having fun and making friends. He learned that playing the trumpet is not everything. He learned that he was foolish to forget other things. He learned that he could try again next time. He learned that he could still win.

But then they saw a problem. There was only one pit in the box. A pit was a toy that looked like a hole. You could put other toys in it and pretend they were hiding or digging. Ben and Lily both wanted the pit. They both reached for it at the same time.

"No, it's mine!" Ben shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Lily shouted.

They pulled and tugged on the pit. They did not want to share. They made a lot of noise.

Mom heard them and came back. She saw them fighting over the pit. She was not happy. She said, "Stop that right now! You are not playing nicely. You are not using your words. You are not sharing. If you can't share the pit, then no one can have it."

She took the pit away from them and put it on a high shelf. She said, "The pit is not available for you until you learn to share. Now you can play with your own toys or you can play together. But you have to be kind and respectful."

Ben and Lily felt sad. They liked the pit. They wished they had shared it. They looked at their own toys. They did not look as fun as the pit. They looked at each other. They felt sorry.

They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We're sorry, Ben. We're sorry, Lily. Can we have the pit back, please?"

Mom smiled. She said, "I'm glad you're sorry. I'm glad you want to share. Yes, you can have the pit back. But you have to promise to take turns and play nicely."

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "We promise, Mom. We promise, Ben. We promise, Lily."

Mom gave them the pit back. They thanked her. They put the pit on the floor. They decided to play together. They put different toys in the pit and took them out. They pretended they were exploring or rescuing. They had a lot of fun. They shared the pit and they shared their smiles.

Anna and Ben shake their heads.

"A lawyer is someone who helps people with the law. The law is a set of rules that everyone has to follow. Sometimes people have problems with the law, and they need a lawyer to help them. A lawyer talks to the judge and the jury and tries to make them understand their side of the story. A lawyer also helps people make agreements and contracts and write wills. A lawyer has to be honest and fair and smart."

Anna and Ben listen to the lawyer. They think he sounds very interesting and important.

"Wow, mister, you do a lot of things. You must be very smart and good," Anna says.

"Yeah, mister, you sound like a hero. You help people with their problems. That's cool," Ben says.

The lawyer smiles. He feels a little warmer and happier. He likes the kids. They are curious and polite.

"Thank you, kids. You are very sweet and nice. You know what? You can keep the badge. It's a gift from me. Maybe one day you can be lawyers too. Or whatever you want to be. Just remember to work hard and follow your dreams."

Anna and Ben are surprised and happy. They thank the lawyer and hug him. They put the badge back on the snowman.

"Look, mister, now our snowman is a lawyer snowman again. But he's also our friend. And he's your friend too," Anna says.

"Yes, mister, he's our friend. And you're our friend too. Thank you for the badge and the story. We learned a lot from you," Ben says.

The lawyer laughs. He feels a little less angry and lonely. He likes the snowman. He's cute and funny.

"You're welcome, kids. You made my day. And you made a great snowman. He's the best lawyer snowman I've ever seen. He's my friend too."

They all smile and wave goodbye. They go their separate ways. But they don't forget each other. They remember the day they met and the snowman they made. They remember the badge and the story. They remember the law and the dream. They remember the friendship and the fun.

They came to the lion enclosure. They saw a big lion lying on a rock. He had a mane and sharp teeth. He looked sleepy. Tim and Sam wanted to see him roar. They got closer to the fence and shouted, "Roar, lion, roar!" The lion opened his eyes and looked at them. He did not roar. He yawned.

Tim and Sam were disappointed. They wanted to hear a loud roar. They shouted again, "Roar, lion, roar!" The lion did not roar. He got up and walked away. He went to a shady spot and lay down again.

Tim and Sam were angry. They wanted to see a real lion, not a lazy lion. They stomped their feet and threw their hats on the ground. They did not see the sign that said, "Do not feed the animals." They did not see the peacock that was walking behind them.

The peacock saw the hats. He liked shiny things. He saw the buttons on the hats. He thought they were jewels. He wanted to have them. He walked to the hats and picked one up with his beak. He turned around and walked away.

Tim and Sam heard a noise. They turned around and saw the peacock. They saw their hat in his mouth. They gasped. They ran after the peacock. They shouted, "Hey, give us back our hat!"

The peacock was scared. He ran faster. He ran into the crowd. He bumped into people and animals. He made a lot of noise. He dropped the hat. He ran away.

Tim and Sam chased the hat. They pushed and shoved. They stumbled and fell. They got up and ran. They caught the hat. They were happy. They put it back on their head.

They looked around. They saw their dad. He was not happy. He was angry. He saw them make a mess. He saw them break the rules. He saw them scare the peacock. He said, "Tim and Sam, what have you done? You have been very naughty. You have made a big mess. You have to say sorry to the people and the animals. You have to leave the zoo now. No more safari for you."

Tim and Sam felt bad. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not mean to be naughty. They said sorry to the people and the animals. They followed their dad to the car. They were quiet and sad. They learned their lesson. They did not shout at the lion anymore. They did not throw their hats anymore. They did not chase the peacock anymore. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We love you. We love the zoo. We love the animals. Can we come back another day?"

Their dad sighed. He was still angry, but he loved them. He said, "Maybe, if you behave better. Now, let's go home and have some lunch. You must be hungry after your messy safari."

Mia takes the paper plane and runs to the window. She throws the paper plane out of the window. But the paper plane does not fly. It falls to the ground.

"Oh no!" Mia says. "The paper plane does not fly. It is too heavy."

"I know!" Tom says. "Let's attach a balloon to the paper plane. A balloon can make the paper plane lighter."

Mia takes the paper plane with the balloon and runs to the window. She throws the paper plane out of the window. The paper plane flies in the air. The balloon lifts the paper plane higher and higher.

Tim and Sam did not know this. They thought the noise was part of the fun. They kept running until they reached their home.

"Wow, Anna, that is a good find!" Ben said. "Can I see it?"

Anna gave Ben the copper. He looked at it closely. He saw the face of a man with a hat and a beard. He wondered who he was.

"Who is this man, Anna?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe he is a king or a hero," Anna said.

"Maybe he is," Ben said. "Do you think he has a name?"

"Maybe his name is Copper," Anna said, giggling.

Ben giggled too. He liked Anna's idea. He raised the copper in the air and said, "Hello, Copper! You are a very nice coin. Thank you for letting us play with you."

Anna raised her hand and waved at the copper. She said, "Hello, Copper! You are a very pretty coin. We are happy to find you."

They heard a voice from the house. It was their mom. She said, "Anna, Ben, it is time to come in. It is getting dark and cold."

"OK, mom, we are coming!" Anna and Ben said. They put the copper in their pocket and ran to the house. They wanted to show their mom their new friend. They hoped she would like Copper too.

One day, Tom and Lily are playing on the screen. They are having fun. They forget to do their homework. They forget to eat their lunch. They forget to listen to their mom and dad. They only want to play on the screen.

Tom's mom comes to the room. She is angry. She sees Tom and Lily on the screen. She says, "Tom, Lily, what are you doing? You forgot to do your homework. You forgot to eat your lunch. You need to stop playing on the screen. You need to do your homework. You need to eat your lunch. You need to listen to me and your dad. Or else, you will have no screen. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily are scared. They say, "Sorry, mom. We are sorry. We forgot. We will do our homework. We will eat our lunch. We will listen to you and dad. Please, don't take away the screen. We love the screen. The screen is fun. The screen is our friend. Please, mom, please."

Tom's mom is not happy. She says, "No, Tom, Lily. You are not sorry. You are not good children. You are addicted to the screen. The screen is not your friend. The screen is your enemy. No screen at all. I will take away the screen. I will lock the screen in the closet. You will never see the screen again. Never. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily are sad. They cry. They say, "No, mom, no. Please, don't take away the screen. Please, don't lock the screen in the closet. Please, let us see the screen. Please, mom, please."

But Tom's mom does not listen. She takes away the screen. She locks the screen in the closet. She leaves the room. She says, "Goodbye, screen. Goodbye, Tom. Goodbye, Lily."

Tom and Lily are alone. They have no screen. They have no fun. They have no friend. They have nothing. They are very sad. They are very sorry. They are very lonely. They wish they did not forget. They wish they were good children. They wish they had the screen. But they have no screen. They have no screen at all. The end.

Tom was a poor boy who lived with his mom in a small house. He did not have many toys or clothes, but he loved his mom very much. Every day, he helped her with the chores and made her smile.

One day, Tom saw a shiny red bike in the window of a shop. He wanted to ride it so badly, but he knew it was too expensive for them. He asked his mom if he could have it, but she shook her head and said, "I'm sorry, Tom, we don't have enough money for that. Maybe someday, when things get better."

Tom felt sad, but he did not cry. He hugged his mom and said, "I love you, mom. You are the best thing I have." His mom smiled and kissed him on the cheek.

The next day, Tom was walking to the park with his mom, when he saw a shiny penny on the ground. He picked it up and showed it to his mom. "Look, mom, I found a penny! Can I keep it?" he asked.

His mom nodded and said, "Sure, Tom, you can keep it. It's your lucky penny. Maybe it will bring you some good fortune."

Tom was happy and put the penny in his pocket. He felt like he had a treasure. He thought maybe he could save up more pennies and buy the bike someday.

When they got to the park, Tom saw a man with a big hat and a long coat. He was playing a guitar and singing songs. People were listening and clapping and giving him coins. Tom liked the music and wanted to join them. He asked his mom if he could go closer.

His mom said, "Okay, Tom, but don't go too far. Stay where I can see you."

Tom nodded and ran to the man. He listened to his songs and clapped along. He felt happy and forgot about his troubles. He looked at the man and saw that he had a kind smile and a friendly voice. He decided to make a request.

He took out his penny and said, "Excuse me, sir, can you please play a song for my mom? She is very nice and works very hard. She deserves a song."

The man looked at Tom and saw his bright eyes and his dirty clothes. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He said, "Of course, little boy, I can play a song for your mom. What is her name?"

Tom said, "Her name is Mary. She is over there, on the bench."

The man nodded and said, "Okay, Tom, this song is for Mary. It's called 'You Are My Sunshine'."

He started to play his guitar and sing the song. Tom smiled and ran back to his mom. He hugged her and said, "Mom, listen, this song is for you. I requested it with my penny."

His mom looked at him and heard the song. She felt a tear roll down her cheek. She said, "Thank you, Tom, you are my sunshine. You are the best thing I have."

They both listened to the song and felt happy. They did not care that they were poor. They had each other and their lucky penny. And they had a song.

The gorilla looked at the boy and grunted. He did not like the noise.

"Hello, gorilla!" the girl said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The gorilla looked at the girl and growled. He did not like the visitors.

The boy and the girl did not understand. They thought the gorilla was friendly. They climbed over the fence and went into the cage. They wanted to touch the gorilla and give him a hug.

The mom saw them and screamed. She ran to the cage and tried to get them out. But it was too late.

The gorilla was angry and scared. He did not want the children in his home. He grabbed the boy and the girl and threw them into a pot. He wanted to cook them and eat them.

The mom cried and shouted for help. The zookeepers came and tried to stop the gorilla. But it was too late.

The gorilla cooked the boy and the girl and ate them. He was full and happy.

The end.

"Look, Cluck, it's a firework!" Lily said. "It's so pretty!"

"Wow, Cluck, you are amazing!" Lily said. "You made a firework chicken!"

Cluck smiled and cuddled with Lily. He was happy that he could share his secret with her. He was a special chicken with a special glow. He loved Lily and she loved him. Sara and Tom are angry. They turn around. They say, "Stop it. You are rude. We like the show. You are ruining it."

The boy does not stop. He says, "No, you stop. You are babies. Puppets are for babies. I want to go."

The puppeteer hears the noise. He stops the show. He looks at the boy. He says, "What is the matter? Why are you making trouble? Why don't you enjoy the show?"

The boy says, "I don't like puppets. They are boring. I want to play something else."

The puppeteer says, "Well, that is a shame. Puppets are fun. They can teach you many things. They can make you laugh and think. They can be your friends. But if you don't like them, you don't have to watch them. You can leave. But you have to be polite. You have to respect the other children who like the show. You have to be quiet and not disturb them. Do you understand?"

The boy nods. He says, "Yes, I understand. I'm sorry. I won't make noise anymore. I will leave."

The puppeteer says, "Thank you. That is very nice of you. I hope you find something else that you like to do. Goodbye."

The boy gets up. He walks out of the tent. He looks for another place to play.

Sara and Tom smile. They say, "Thank you, puppeteer. You are very kind. We love your show. Can we see more?"

The puppeteer says, "Of course. You are very welcome. I'm glad you like my show. I have more puppets to show you. Are you ready?"

Sara and Tom say, "Yes, we are ready."

The puppeteer says, "Okay, then. Let's continue. Here comes the next puppet. It is a lion. He is very brave and strong. But he has a problem. He has a thorn in his paw. He needs help. Who will help him?"

Sara and Tom watch. They are curious. They want to see what happens. They clap their hands. They enjoy the show.

The bird looked at Tom and chirped softly. It felt warm and safe in his arms. It was glad that Tom found it. It said, "Thank you, kind fisherman. You are very brave and good. You are my friend now."

Tom smiled and hugged the bird. He felt happy and not lonely anymore. He said, "You are welcome, little bird. You are very sweet and smart. You are my friend too."

They sailed together to Tom's house. They ate some fish and bread. They made a nest for the bird. They told each other stories and jokes. They became the best of friends. They were never lonely again.

She finds many matches and has a big pile of cards. Ben is not so good at remembering. He finds only a few matches and has a small pile of cards.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous of your friends. Be happy for their talents and learn from them. And don't let a game ruin your friendship. Play fair and have fun.

The human came back and saw the mess and the dogs. He was angry and sad. He shouted at them and took them to the vet. Sara put on her coat and ran to the garden. She saw the pumpkin was bigger than her head. She touched it and felt it was hard and smooth. She saw the vine had green leaves and yellow flowers. She also saw some prickles that looked sharp. She was careful not to touch them.

She said to the pumpkin, "Hello, pumpkin. You are very big and orange. Do you like to grow in the garden? Do you like to be a pie or a soup or a face?"
